On of the CIT strategic goals and objectives was to build capacity in emerging areas of interest such as AI and DS.
This  has  been worked  on  for  few years,  and  CIT  continued  the  effort  during  the  24/25  academic year  by  hiring
several faculty members with strong research profiles in these areas. Another strategic goal was to update under-
graduate and graduate programs making them more relevant to market needs. This has been a work-in-progress
task   which   will    continue    through    the    next    academic   year.   With    respect    to    students’    needs,    it   was    strategically
important for the CIT to improve the advising process and time to graduation. This has been worked on and will
continue during the next academic year. Internship during the summer term was implemented which helped stu-
dents  to  graduate  one  term  earlier,  and  proactive  advising was  implemented  to  identify  students  at  risk  to  help
them cope with any challenges.

The   CIT  will   continue   to  work   on   making   improvements   to   its   programs,   create   new   interdisciplinary   programs
such as the one in Cognitive Science and AI with the CHSS and will continue to find better ways to serve students
and   faculty.   CIT   needs   to   improve   its   outreach   and   collaboration   with   industry   to   attract   external   funding   and
build more partnerships with industry. In addition, CIT will aim to further enhance research productivity of faculty
by hiring more faculty to reduce the teaching load to its normal values and cope with the increasing number of
students’ intake.

Enrollment  trends  across  the  College  of  Information Technology  over  the  past  six  academic years  reflect  steady
growth with periodic fluctuations across all programs. In the Bachelor of Science (BSc) Programs, student enroll-
ment per year (intake), Figure1, increased consistently from approximately 500 in AY2020-21 to a peak of about
750 in AY2022-23, indicating a significant rise in student interest during that period. This growth was followed by
a gradual decline to around 630 students in AY2023-24 and approximately 500 in AY2024-25, before recovering
to about 670 students in AY2025-26. Overall, the BSc Programs have maintained a strong level of participation,
demonstrating continued appeal among undergraduate students despite minor year-to-year variations.

A     similar     pattern     of     fluctuation     can     be     observed     in     the     Master     Programs,    where     enrollment     per    year     (intake),
Figure   2,   rose   from   around   27   students   in  AY2020-21   to   a   peak   of   35   in  AY2021-22,   before   declining   sharply
to  approximately  13  in AY2022-23. The  following years  showed  a  positive  recovery, with  enrollment  increasing
again to about 35 students in AY2024-25, followed by a moderate decrease to around 22 in AY2025-26. These
shifts suggest variable demand for graduate studies, possibly influenced by external factors such as employment
trends, scholarship opportunities, or post-pandemic academic adjustments.

The   Doctor   of   Philosophy   (Ph.D.)   Program   has   shown   steady   and   encouraging   enrollment   trends   over   the   past
six academic years. Starting with around a total enrollment, Figure 3, of 55 students in AY2020-21, the program
experienced    consistent    growth,    reaching    its    highest    point    of    approximately    80    students    in  AY2022-23.    Enroll-
ment remained strong in the following years, with about 75 students in AY2023-24 and 65 in AY2024-25, before
stabilizing at around 50 students in AY2025-26 while focusing on better quality students. These figures highlight
the  program’s  sustained  appeal  and  the  continued  commitment  of  students  to  pursuing  advanced  research  and
academic excellence within the College of Information Technology.

During the 2024-2025 academic
years there were few major chal-
lenges. One of the challenges was
coping up with the increase of
number of admitted undergraduate
students in terms of scheduling the
courses         needed,         advising         and         hir-
ing faculty to cover up the needed
teaching load. Another major chal-
lenge   was    related    to    attracting    top
candidates to hire as faculty mem-
bers    due    to    the    fierce    competition
from     other     institutions     in     the     UAE
and           the           GCC.           In           addition,           it          was
challenging to cope with the fre-
quent request, which are always needed urgently, for data from various University entities due to the lack of any
systematic approach to collect such data ahead of time. This created a stressful environment for faculty members
and staff.  Moreover, one of the main challenges was related to the bureaucracy and lengthy process of purchas-
ing equipment needed by the College and in getting approvals for conducting or participating in certain activities.

The College made significant strides in advancing its strategic goals during 2024–2025, with major achievements
across academic excellence, research innovation, and global engagement. CBE successfully diversified its student
and faculty base, strengthened its academic offerings, and expanded its research portfolio, positioning itself as a
regional leader in business education and policy-relevant scholarship. Through renewed partnerships and newly
established collaborations, the College deepened its engagement with industry and academia both regionally and
internationally, reinforcing its role as a hub of knowledge creation and application.

Key accomplishments this year included surpassing publication targets, expanding external research grants, and
broadening   faculty   participation   in   funded   projects.  The   College Annual   Research   Program   (CARP)   has   evolved
into   a  vibrant   platform   that   now   actively   involves   students   alongside   faculty   members,   fostering   early   research
engagement  and  experiential  learning.  Collaborative  initiatives  such  as  the  Ministry  of  Economy’s  Business  Re-
search Network and the Statistics Centre Abu Dhabi (SCAD) micro-credential program have further strengthened
the  link  between  academic  inquiry  and  national  development  goals. The  College  also  continued  to  align  its  cur-
ricula   with    emerging    market    needs    through    the    launch    and    modernization    of    six    academic    programs,    ensuring
graduates are equipped with the skills required for the dynamic global economy.

The    establishment    of    an    International    Coordinator    role,    the    initiation    of    high-impact    interdisciplinary    projects,
and  sustained  partnerships with  leading  global  institutions  such  as  Peking  University,  HKUST  (Guangzhou),  and

## PDF page 176 — continuation 2
Beijing     Jiaotong      University      exemplify      CBE’s      growing      international      presence.     These      developments      underscore
the  College’s  ongoing  commitment  to  excellence,  innovation,  and  global  relevance,  enhancing  its visibility  in  in-
ternational  rankings  and  expanding  its  contribution  to  economic  and  societal  advancement  across  the  UAE  and
beyond.

The  College  intends  to  move  toward  HyFlex  learning,  and  accordingly,  the  Dean  approved  in  2024  a  budget  of
AED  286,000  to  equip  one  classroom  at  the Abu  Dhabi  Off-Campus  Site with  advanced  technology  to  support
HyFlex delivery of postgraduate programs.




Addition of New Programs and Update of Existing Programs

Seven    newly    revamped    programs    were    introduced    during    2024–2025,    including    the    MBA,    BBA    in    Marketing,
BBA  in  Entrepreneurship,  BBA  in  Human  Resource  Management,  BBA  in  Supply  Chain  Management  and  Logis-
tics, the Bachelor of Economics and the DBA program. In addition, the revamping of the MPA programs has also
been done.

Accreditation and assessment outcomes:

All      CBE      undergraduate      and      postgraduate      programs     were      reaccredited      by      both     AACSB      and      CAA,      following      a
successful    combined    review    in    February    2024.  The    College    has    also    applied    for    EQUIS    accreditation,   with    the
first review visit scheduled for early 2026. Prof. Madi and Dr. Mayada remain actively engaged with AACSB. Prof.
Madi   is   an  AACSB   mentor   for   three   business   schools,   serves   as   a   reviewer   and   a   member   of   the  AACSB   Initial
Accreditation Committee, and Dr. Mayada El-Hadidi serves as a Reviewer and Member of the Accounting Accred-
itation Committee.

## PDF page 200
Program Accreditation Report

CAA   Accreditation.     With    regard    to    accreditation,    the    current    academic   year    has    been    a    highly    successful    one
for CHSS. In December 2024, the college submitted extensive documentation to the Commission for Academic
Accreditation (CAA) in support of its application for reaccreditation of all programs. In March 2025, we hosted a
CAA External Review Team which conducted a comprehensive review of sixteen of the programs offered by the
college,  with   two  programs  being  exempt. The  result   of  this  review  was  that  all  sixteen  programs  under  review
were   approved   for   reaccreditation.   Indeed,   the   college   was   commended    for   the   overall   quality   of   its   academic
provision and the manner in which its programs were aligned with CAA Standards. The UAEU places a high pri-
ority on both national and international accreditation. Accordingly, the above outcomes are something of which
the college can rightly be proud.

The    Commission    has    approved    the    UAEU   Applications    for    Renewal    of    Program   Accreditation    of    the    following
programs.

 1.      MASTER OF SOCIAL WORK
 2.      BACHELOR OF SOCIAL WORK
 3.      BACHELOR OF SCIENCE IN APPLIED SOCIOLOGY AND SOCIAL DATA ANALYTICS
 4.      MASTER OF ARTS IN ENGLISH
 5.      BACHELOR OF ARTS IN ENGLISH LITERATURE
 6.      BACHELOR OF ARTS IN LINGUISTICS
 7.      BACHELOR OF ARTS IN TRANSLATION STUDIES
 8.      BACHELOR OF ARTS IN MASS COMMUNICATION
 9.      MASTER OF ARTS IN COMMUNICATION
 10.   MASTER OF SCIENCE IN REMOTE SENSING AND GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEMS
 11.   MASTER OF GOVERNANCE AND PUBLIC POLICY
 12.   BACHELOR OF ARTS IN POLITICAL SCIENCE
 13.   BACHELOR OF ARTS IN VISUAL STUDIES AND CREATIVE INDUSTRIES
 14.   BACHELOR OF ARTS IN PSYCHOLOGY
 15.   BACHELOR OF ARTS IN ARABIC LANGUAGE AND LITERATURE
 16.   MASTER OF ARTS IN ARABIC LANGUAGE AND LITERATURE


International  Accreditation.    In   addition   to   the   success   of   the   CAA   accreditation  visit,   three   more   programs   re-
ceived  international  accreditation via AQAS,  in  Germany. The  three  programs were  the  BA  in  English  Literature
and the BA in Translation Studies, hosted by the Department of Languages and Literature and the BA in Linguis-
tics, hosted by the Department of Cognitive Sciences. The BA in Tourism  Studies was internationally accredited
by   the   UNWTO.TedQual. The   UNWTO   (World Tourism   Organization)   is   a   specialized   agency   of   the   United   Na-
tions. For this reason, it was exempted from the CAA program review and given full accreditation.

bility, geospatial science, urban development, and public policy, as follows:

Research Partnerships:   Research  partnerships  are  essential  for  fostering  scholarly  collaboration,  enhancing  in-
stitutional      reputations,      and      promoting      the      exchange      of      knowledge      and      expertise.      In      May      2025,      Dr.    Amna    Al
Ahbabi  from  the  United Arab  Emirates  University  (UAEU)  initiated  a  strategic  academic  collaboration with  King
Saud University by applying for a visiting scholar position as part of a research sabbatical proposal. In recognition
of    the    potential    for    mutual    benefit,    King    Saud    University    extended    a    formal    invitation    to    Dr.  Al  Ahbabi    to    join
their  institution  as  a visiting  scholar. This  invitation  underscores  the  shared  commitment  of  both  universities  to
advance     academic     cooperation     through     joint     research     efforts,     co-authored     publications,     and     the     exchange     of
best    practices.    Subsequently,    UAEU    approved    Dr.   Al   Ahbabi’s    sabbatical    request,    granting    her    full    benefits    for
the 2025–2026 academic year. This partnership represents a significant step in strengthening cross-institutional
research networks and contributes to the internationalization of UAEU’s academic endeavors.able resources for
teaching, scholarship, and cultural engagement.

6. Elevate Institutional Reputation and Global Competitiveness.

Significantly  improve  research  productivity,  including  publications  in Top  1%, Top  10%, Top  25%  and  cita-
tions by 15 % every year.


Deliver at least three (3) new or expanded academic programs aligned with national priorities by 2029 and
increase graduate employability and on-time graduation rates by 2% yearly through flexible internship and
proactive academic advising.


Strengthen  CEDU’s  community  engagement  by  increasing  our  LLL  initiatives  to  5% yearly  equipping  indi-
viduals    with     relevant     skills    through     diverse    educational    pathways,    while     promoting    community    develop-
ment and sustainability.


Achieve 95% of all our KPI targets for 2025-2029.

College Infrastructure.
College Facilities and Laboratories

The  College  of  Education  maintains  a  safe,  healthy  and  attractive  campus  environment  for  its  students,  faculty,
staff and visitors in Al Ain. The main campus is a state-of-the-art futuristic model campus complete with all mod-
ern amenities and the latest cutting-edge technology to support the needs of the University’s teaching, research
and service mission.
Early Childhood Education Laboratory:




















Early childhood Education lab is a place where the students get to learn how a regular room in preschool or Kin-
dergartens might look. The lab is equipped with different materials and theme corners. The materials and corners
such as literacy and numeracy corner, reading corner, arts and crafts corner, exploration corner, tradition corner
and Bakery corner, allow the students to engage in different activities while practicing for future calls. The lab is
located in C1 building room 0013.
Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics Education Laboratory
STEM  Laboratory:




















STEAM Lab is built on the integrated approach to learning that combines Science, Technology, Engineering, Art,
and Math. It aims to develop the teaching and learning skills of Early Childhood Mathematics and Science student
teachers. The lab is equipped with hands-on materials for students to engage in activities which can be used for
their planning and preparation of lessons for future. This is intended for them to assist their students to have fun
exploring  science,  technology,  engineering,  and  math  (STEAM)  to  solve  real-world  problems with  creativity  and
critical thinking. The lab is located in C1 building room 0048.


23 0

## PDF page 231
Physical Education Biomechanics Laboratory:

















This is the first Exercise Physiology  and Biomechanics Laboratories in the country. This laboratory is a specialized
facility designed to study the mechanical aspects of human movement and the physical forces involved in various
activities.    It    is    equipped   with    motion    capture    systems    that    precisely    record    the    movements    of    individuals    and
high-speed cameras to capture rapid movements.  The lab is located in F3 building room 020.
Physical Education Laboratory

















This     lab     is     designed     to     help     students     explore,     discover,     and     collect     data     related     to     students’     projects.     It     ena-
bles    students    to    evaluate    health-related    components    of    physical    fitness.   To    enable    students    to    complete    their
projects,    it    is    equipped    with    tools    related    to    exercise    testing,    metabolic    measurements,    cardiovascular    system
function assessment, strength, endurance, and flexibility testing, also it provides the opportunity to assess body
composition.  The lab is located in C1 building room 0031.
Special Education, Child  & Family  Laboratory

their  full  potential.    In  addition,  child  and  family  lab  supports  the  community  by  offering  consultations  and  ses-
sions related to children's disabilities.

ening impactful research, and serving the community through strong national and international partnerships. The
accomplishments      below      reflect      the      College’s      collective      commitment      to      academic      excellence,      innovation,      and
societal contribution.

Academic Programs and Curriculum
New programs or courses introduced
A total of eight new courses have been introduced in the Bachelor of Law program for two main reasons. The first
is   to   respond   to   the   recent   reforms   in   the   General   Education   Program   requirements,   through   the   introduction
of   two   courses:  Advanced  Arabic   Language   Skills   for   Law   and   Legal  Terminology   in   English.  These   courses   aim
to enhance students’ academic  language proficiency in alignment with the program’s language of instruction,  in
accordance   with    the    approved    revisions    and    the    Commission    for   Academic   Accreditation    (CAA)    guidelines    on
“Academic Language Proficiency.”

The   second   reason   relates   to   the   revision,   separation,   and   merging   of   certain   courses   as   part   of   the   program’s
reaccreditation process. The newly introduced courses under this category include: Selected Studies in Compar-
ative Law, Voluntary Sources of Obligation, Non-Voluntary Sources of Obligation, Criminal Law and Penalties (1),
Criminal Law and Penalties (2), Public Finance and Tax Legislation.

As for the postgraduate programs, the matter remains under review, as these programs are currently being eval-
uated by the Agency for Quality Assurance (AQAS) in preparation for obtaining international accreditation.

It is worth noting that the College has launched a new Minor Program in “Law for Engineering” designed for stu-
dents  of  the  College  of  Engineering. This  program  aims  to  equip  students with  foundational  knowledge  in  legal
issues related to engineering practices, contracts, and patents, thereby providing them with a competitive edge
in the job market. The program has witnessed significant interest within only three academic semesters since its
introduction, as indicated by preliminary statistics.

updated and enhanced the curricula of all its academic pro-
grams. The  revision  covered  64  courses, whose  descriptions
and    content   were    reviewed    to    reflect    recent    legislative,    so-
cial,   and   technological   developments,   and   to   strengthen   the
integration between theoretical and practical aspects of legal
education.

In   addition,   the   learning   outcomes   of   all   programs  were   up-
dated     to     align    with     the     new     National     Qualifications     Frame-

Accreditation and assessment outcomes
In   2024,   the   College   successfully   renewed   the   national   accreditation   for   all   its   programs   through   the   Commis -
sion    for   Academic   Accreditation    (CAA),    reaffirming     its     strong    commitment     to    the     highest     standards    of    quality
and academic excellence. The Bachelor of Law program also obtained international accreditation from the High
Council for Evaluation of Research and Higher Education (HCERES) in France—an outstanding achievement that
strengthens the College’s international academic standing and validates the quality of its educational outcomes.
Currently, the College is working toward obtaining international accreditation for its postgraduate programs from
the Agency for Quality Assurance (AQAS), as part of its continuous pursuit of global recognition.

The College places great emphasis on measuring program learning outcomes annually through approved assess-
ment  cycles  designed  to  evaluate  the  extent  to which  intended  learning  outcomes  are  achieved  and  to  identify
areas requiring corrective action. During the 2024/2025 academic year, the College initiated the fourth assess-
ment   cycle   for   the   Bachelor   of   Law   program,   completed   the   fifth   cycle   for   both   the   Master   of   Public   Law   and
Master of Private Law programs, and concluded the second cycle for the PhD in Law program.
To  ensure  continuous  quality  enhancement,  the  College  systematically  evaluates various  aspects  of  the  educa -
tional process across its programs through several mechanisms, including:

  •                                   Regularly     sur veying     stakeholders     (student s,     graduates,     and     employers)     to     collect     feedback     on     program
     learning outcomes.
  •                                   Developing a Program Per formance Improvement Plan by analyzing per formance indicators provided by
     the    Office    of    Institutional    Effec tiveness,    such    as    graduation    timelines,    student    satisfac tion,    enrollment,
     and attrition rates, to identif y areas for improvement.
  •                                   Periodically  reviewing  the  application  of  interac tive  teaching  methods  adopted  by  the  College  to  ensure
     their effec tiveness in fostering ac tive learning.
  •                                   Conduc ting    regular    analyses    of    student    per formance    across    different    courses    to    identif y    streng ths    and
     areas needing suppor t.
  •                                   Collecting       peer       feedback       on       teaching       to       encourage       professional       reflection       and       enhance       instructional
     qualit y.
  •                          Engaging employers in reviewing academic program development plans in alignment with labor market
     requirement s through the College Advisor y Board.

College / Subjects Ranking
There has been a notable improvement in the QS World University Rankings by Subject for Law, with the ranking
rising  from  the  351–370  band  in  2024  to  the  301–350  band  in  2025. This  advancement  reflects   the  College’s
continuous    efforts    to    enhance    the    quality    of    education,    advance    scientific    research,    and    strengthen    academic
engagement with distinguished international experiences.

Research and Innovation

During   the   2024/2025   academic  year,   the   College   observed   that   its   research   publication   output   in   Scopus-in-
dexed journals had not yet reached the targeted benchmark. This situation was influenced by several factors, in-
cluding changes in faculty classification and the corresponding adjustments to publication requirements. As part
of   its   corrective   measures,   the   College   has   appointed   new   faculty   members  with   outstanding   research   records
to strengthen future research productivity. As a result of these measures, the number of research publications in
Scopus-indexed journals has increased to 47, exceeding expectations for the current academic year.

To promote Arab academic and research collaboration, the College organized the Annual International Research
Competition    for    Law    Faculty    Members    in   Arab    Universities,    which     reached    its    sixth    edition    in    2024/2025.    In
addition,      to      enhance      research      capacity      and      productivity,      the      College      intensified      efforts      to      encourage      faculty
members   to   apply   for   competitive   research   grants,  with   four   funded   research   projects   during   the  year. Among
the most notable was the UAE University Transformation Research Program grant in partnership with McGill Uni-
versity,          titled          “CRISPR-Cas9         Technology:         Advancing          Gene
Editing and Exploring Its Ethical and Legal Dimensions.”

Another key project was conducted for the Family Devel-
opment      Foundation,      titled      “The      Legal      Protection      of      Senior
Citizens in the United Arab Emirates: Envisioning the Future
from     a     Comparative     Perspective,”     an     applied     research     initi-
ative    that    integrates    academic    rigor   with    societal    impact    to
serve national priorities.

In   the   field   of   academic   publications,   the   College,   in   collab-
oration   with    the    Sharjah   Academy    for    Education,    published
a  distinguished  scholarly  book  titled  “Legal  Frameworks  and
Educational         Strategies         for         Sustainable         Development.”        This
comprehensive academic reference addresses contemporary
challenges in achieving sustainable development through the
integration     of     legal     frameworks     and     educational     strategies.
The     book     bridges     environmental     law,     sustainability     studies,
and innovative educational practices, offering a multidisciplinary perspective that connects theory with practice

## PDF page 264 — continuation 2
and    provides    policymakers   with    practical,    evidence-based    tools.   The    book   was    officially    indexed    in    Scopus    on
June    14,    2025,    reinforcing    its    credibility    as    a    trusted    reference    for    scholars    in    law,    education,    and    sustainable
development.

As   part   of   its   institutional   collaboration   efforts,   the  year   2025  witnessed   the   completion   of   the   Guidelines   for
Determining Criminal Penalties for Commercial Companies Project, developed by the College in partnership with
the Supreme Legislation Committee in Dubai. This initiative is expected to have a major positive impact by sup -
porting    the    judiciary    in    adjudicating    corporate   violations,    enhancing    the    business    environment,    and    advancing
the legislative and judicial framework in the Emirate.

In     its     ongoing     commitment     to     fostering     academic     and     research     excellence,     the     College     annually     presents     Ex-
cellence Awards  to  faculty  members  in  recognition  of  their  achievements  in  research,  teaching,  and  community
service, thereby promoting a culture of innovation, quality, and positive academic competition.

Success Stories of Alumni
Lama Abu Mahmoud stands out as one of the College of Law’s distinguished alumni, recognized for her outstand-
ing academic excellence and active participation in various college initiatives. She received a prestigious job offer
from   the   Legal  Affairs   Department   at Yango   Group   International   and   is   currently   pursuing   her   Master’s   degree
in  Private  Law  offered  by  the  College.  Lama  also  made  a  remarkable  research  contribution  by  authoring  a  book
chapter      in      “Legal      Frameworks      and      Educational      Strategies      for      Sustainable      Development,”      a      publication      jointly
issued by the College and the Sharjah Academy for Education, which was indexed in Scopus on June 14, 2025.

Shamma Al  Niyadi,  a  graduate  of  the  2024/2025  academic year,  distinguished  herself  through  exceptional  aca-
demic performance and active participation in the Willem C. Vis International Commercial Arbitration Moot for
two consecutive years. She received an honorable mention at the 14th Annual Middle East Pre-Moot organized
by the Bahrain Chamber for Dispute Resolution (BCDR). Shamma is currently employed at the Abu Dhabi Global
Market Authority (ADGM Authority), where she continues to build a promising career in the legal sector.

## PDF page 266
Community Engagement and Service
The   College   of   Law   has   been   committed   to   fostering   community   engagement   through   a  wide   range   of   educa-
tional    programs    and    training    initiatives    designed    to    serve    diverse    segments    of    society,    thereby    reinforcing    the
concept of lifelong learning adopted by the United Arab Emirates University.

During   the   2024/2025   academic  year,   the   College   delivered   approximately   50   community-oriented   programs,
including specialized professional training sessions for lawyers in collaboration with the Judicial Training Institute
of the Ministry of Justice, and training programs for members of the Public Prosecution at the Abu Dhabi Judicial
Department, as part of its strategic partnerships with key judicial authorities in the UAE.

The College also organized a series of seminars, lectures, and workshops with practical training sessions in collab-
oration with international law firms, such as Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner, Hadler & Partner, Clyde & Co, and Al
Tamimi & Company, as well as in partnership with the Abu Dhabi Federal Court of Appeal, the Abu Dhabi Judicial
Department, and the Dubai Courts.

Moreover, the College continued to operate its Legal Clinic with high efficiency, providing free legal consultations
to  various   community   groups   in   areas   such   as   personal   status,   contracts,   commercial   law,   and   civil   law.   It   also
organized legal awareness lectures in schools to promote legal literacy among students and familiarize them with
their rights and obligations, thereby contributing to building a generation that values justice and understands the
pivotal role of law in ensuring social stability and fairness.

 Challenges and Lessons Learned
 The introduction of the MoHESR 24-KPI Performance Framework within a short implementation period present-
 ed several challenges for higher education institutions. The College required additional time to align its internal
 data   systems   and   reporting   mechanisms  with   the   new   national   indicators.  The   limited   timeframe   also   affected
 data  availability  and  consistency,  particularly  for  longitudinal  measures  such  as  graduate  employability,  learning
 outcomes,  and  research  impact.  Furthermore,  the  rapid  rollout  demanded  intensive  capacity-building  efforts  to
 familiarize faculty and administrators with the new metrics.

## PDF page 281
The transformation into a research- intensive university marks a significant milestone in the evolution of United
Arab   Emirates   University   (UAEU).  This   transition   represents    a   commitment    to   advancing    knowledge,   fostering
innovation, and contributing substantially to the global academic landscape. Research-intensive universities are
characterized by their dedication to cutting-edge research across diverse disciplines, their emphasis on fostering
a vibrant intellectual community, and their pivotal role in shaping the future through groundbreaking discoveries
and inventions.

UAEU   is   becoming,   more   than   ever   before,   a   dynamic   institute  with   a  wide   range   of   interdisciplinary   scholarly
activities. UAEU has launched its new Research and Innovation Strategy (RIS) for the cycle 2023-26 to transform
its     research     ecosystem,     and     to     find     innovative     solutions     to     21st-century     problems     both     at     home     and     abroad.
This  new  RIS  comprises  14  projects  under  5  key  strategic  goals  that  have  been  developed  in  collaboration with
the university stakeholders and partners in the community. This comprehensive strategy underlines the UAEU’s
commitment to generating a positive social impact and advancing the knowledge-based economy of the UAE.

UAEU     Faculty     member     from     College     of     Engineering     Explores     Groundwater     Storage     Dynamics     in    Abu     Dhabi
Using AI Technique

Dr. Khaled Al Ghafli, Assistant Professor at the College of Engineering, UAE University, has developed an innova-
tive study aimed at understanding the dynamics of groundwater storage across the Abu Dhabi Emirate and iden-
tifying the key factors influencing groundwater level fluctuations. His research integrates hydrological data with
satellite-based  observations  and  uses  machine  learning  techniques  to  develop  a  model  that  predicts  changes  in

## PDF page 284 — continuation 2
groundwater  storage. This  is  the  first  study  of  its  kind  in  the  region  to  apply  artificial  intelligence  techniques  to
predict temporal variations in groundwater storage. The study was conducted in collaboration with the Environ-
ment Agency – Abu Dhabi (EAD), which played a crucial role in validating satellite data and testing the developed
model.    In    addition,    collaboration   with    researchers    from    the    University    of    Glasgow    (Scotland)    and   Wageningen
University (the Netherlands) further strengthened the research outcomes and enhanced the study’s international
dimension.

Understanding      multiple      sclerosis:    The      search      for      an-
swers to an epidemiological puzzle

The       global       prevalence       of       multiple       sclerosis       is       on       the
rise,  and  this  has  serious  consequences  for  those who
live with the disease and our healthcare systems. At
the       United     Arab       Emirates       University,       researchers       are
building a profile of the disease by studying risk factors
such as Epstein-Barr virus and low vitamin D levels.

## PDF page 287
Strategic  Research Themes

Health and Medical Sciences (HMS)

UAEU is at the forefront of health innovation, focusing
on improving human health and quality of life. UAEU’s
health    research    focuses    on    tackling    critical    challenges
such  as  obesity,  oncology,  and  infectious  diseases,  ad-
dressing pressing global and regional health concerns.
Studies   on   adverse   pregnancy   outcomes,   such   as   pre-
term           births,           aim           to           improve           maternal           and           neonatal
health.           Cutting-edge           innovations           like           cuffless           blood
pressure    monitoring    devices    enhance    patient    comfort
and accuracy, while ongoing work on infectious disease
prevention        and        cancer        therapies        exemplifies        UAEU's
dedication   to   advancing   healthcare   for   a   healthier   so-
ciety.




Space Science and Technology (SST)

UAEU’s   space   science   and   technology   research   drives
sustainable economic growth by fostering collabora-
tion   between   government,   private,   and   academic   sec-
tors.         Key         areas         include          earth         observation,         planetary
science,    and    spacecraft    data    analysis,   with    a    focus    on
addressing issues like land cover changes and climate
monitoring.     These      initiatives      contribute      to      advancing
the UAE’s position as a leader in space exploration and
STEM-based education.




Water, Energy, Food, and Agriculture Sus-
tainability (WEFAS)

UAEU researchers are addressing global sustainability
challenges by developing innovative solutions in water,
energy,     food,     and     agriculture     systems.     Enhancements
in  rainfall  prediction  models  for  arid  regions,  sustaina-
ble residential energy consumption, and the production
of jet fuel from halophytes reflect UAEU’s commitment
to  environmental  stewardship.  Collaborative  efforts  in
plant-based meat development and sustainable agri-
culture further demonstrate the university’s leadership
in building a resilient and sustainable future.

## PDF page 290
United  Arab    Emirates    University    (UAEU)    plays    a    leading    role    in    advancing    the    United    Nations    Sustainable    De-
velopment  Goals  (SDGs)  in  alignment with  the  UAE’s  national  sustainability  agenda. Through  high-impact,  solu-
tion-driven research, UAEU addresses critical global and national challenges in areas such as clean water, renew-
able energy, green mobility, and sustainable agriculture, reinforcing its position as a hub for sustainability-focused
innovation.

In   alignment  with   the   UAE’s   national   ethos   and   commitment   to   sustainable   development   goals,   UAEU   embed-
ded sustainability across research, education, and community engagement activities.. The University significant-
ly     expanded     the     number     of     SDG-focused     research     projects,     particularly     at     the     undergraduate     level,     fostering
early  student  involvement  in  applied  sustainability  research.  Reflecting  this  commitment,  approximately  44%  of
UAEU’s   publications   in   2025   addressed   one   or   more   SDGs,   demonstrating   strong   alignment   between   research
output and global development priorities.

UAEU’s  impact  has  been  recognized  internationally. According  to  the Times  Higher  Education  Impact  Rankings
2025, UAEU was ranked across 12 Sustainable Development Goals, highlighting the breadth of its contributions.
In addition, UAEU ranked number one in the UAE in the QS Sustainability Rankings, underscoring its leadership
in environmental, social, and governance performance.

At the international level, UAEU expanded its SDG Research Program through strategic collaborations with Baku
Engineering    University    and  Azerbaijan    State    Oil    and    Industry    University    in  Azerbaijan.    UAEU    further    strength-
ened    its    global    sustainability    engagement    by    actively    participating    in    COP29    in    Baku,    contributing    to    multiple
panel discussions and high-level meetings focused on climate action and sustainable development.

Education     remains     a     core     pillar     of     UAEU’s     sustainability     strategy.   The     University     launched     a     Minor     in     Climate
Change   and   Sustainability   and   a   Minor   in   Environmental   Engineering,   equipping   students  with   interdisciplinary
knowledge  and  practical  skills  to  address  climate  and  environmental  challenges. These  academic  programs  pre-
pare      future-ready      graduates      to      contribute      meaningfully      to      sustainability-driven      research,      industry,      and      policy
initiatives.

UAEU also demonstrated strong national commitment by supporting the “Plant the Emirates” initiative, funding
27  student  research  projects  that  contribute  directly  to  environmental  protection  and  sustainable  development
within   the   UAE.  Through   integrated   efforts   in   research,   education,   international   collaboration,   and   community
engagement,  UAEU  continues to advance sustainable  solutions  and support  the  UAE’s leadership  in global sus-
tainability efforts.

## PDF page 298
Overview

The National Space Science and Technology Center (NSSTC)
was established in 2016 through the strategic support of
UAE University and the UAE Space Agency, with a clear man-
date  to  advance  the  UAE’s  capabilities  in  Earth  Observation
and   Positioning,   Navigation,   and Timing   (PNT)   technologies.
NSSTC  leads  the  design,  development,  and  operation  of  ad-
vanced satellite missions that align with national priorities.

At the heart of NSSTC’s mission is a leadership driven strate-
gic mindset that focuses on bridging academia and industry
accelerating      innovation     while      ensuring      the      development      of
local     expertise     in     high-technology     sectors.    The     Center     pro-
vides      hands-on      access      to      real      space      missions,      empowering
students, researchers, and engineers to contribute directly to
mission success.

## PDF page 301
Assembly, Integration, and Testing (AIT) Facility
The Assembly,  Integration,  and Testing  (AIT)  Facility  at  the  National  Space  Science  and Technology  Center  (NS  -
STC)   stands   as   one   of   the   UAE’s   most   advanced   space   centers   for   satellite   development   and   qualification.   It   is
established to strengthen the nation’s capabilities in space missions and scientific research, providing end-to-end
support for satellite assembly, environmental testing, and performance validation.

Every step from assembly to integration and environmental testing is performed with rigorous attention to inter-
national space quality and safety standards, ensuring mission success under real space conditions.

The  facility  is  operated  by  a  team  of  certified  Emirati  specialist,  trained  and  qualified  by Airbus with  over  1,000
hours of hands-on operational training. Their technical expertise and commitment to excellence ensure that each
mission delivers satellites ready to perform flawlessly in orbit.

Main Facilities
Our AIT  infrastructure  supports  satellites  up  to  350  kg,  incorporating  advanced  systems  for  environmental  and
functional testing across multiple disciplines:

•                                   L arge     and     Small     Thermal     Vacuum     Chamber     (LT VAC     -     ST VAC):     Simulates     the     vacuum     and     temperature
   ex tremes of space to ensure satellite per formance and reliabilit y under real mission conditions.
•                                   Vibration Shaker: Reproduces the intense launch vibrations to confirm the satellite’s structural integrit y.
•                                   Mass Proper ties Measurement (MPM): Accurately determines the satellite’s center of gravit y and mass for
   launch readiness verification.
•                                   Climatic     Chamber:     Offers     controlled     temperature     and     humidit y     environment s     to     assess     aerospace     and
   space specimens' endurance under var ying terrestrial conditions.

Laboratories
To complement these facilities, the AIT facility includes specialized laboratories designed to support all stages of
assembly, integration and testing:

•                                   Mechanical L aborator y: For mechanical assembly, component fitting, and structural inspec tion.
•                                   Thermal L aborator y: For thermal analysis, temperature control studies, and preconditioning.
•                                   Electrical L aborator y: For electrical integration, inter face checks, and func tional verification.

Today,     NSSTC     proudly     have     15     qualified     Emirati   AIT     special-
ists  who   have   actively   contributed   to   several   national   and   in-
ternational    space    missions.    Supported    the    813   Arab    Satellite
Mission, performing +360 hours of environmental testing and
+160      hours      of      functional      testing      during      the    AIT      phase.      Col-
laborated     with      MBRSC      on     the      Rashid     Rover     2     mission,      con-
tributing to its environmental testing campaign. In addition to

Ground Segment Overview
The Ground Segment at the National Space Science and Technology Center (NSSTC) continues to be the core of
satellite operations for the UAE. Strategically located at the UAE University in Al Ain, the facility ensures contin-
uous communication, tracking, and control of all NSSTC-managed missions.

Equipped   with   advanced   antennas   and   automated   tracking   systems,   the   Ground   Segment   supports  Telemetry,
Tracking,  and  Command  (TT&C)  for  Low  Earth  Orbit  (LEO)  and  Medium  Earth  Orbit  (MEO)  satellites.  It  enables
the   seamless   exchange   of   mission   data   between   spacecraft   and   Earth,   ensuring   successful   satellite   operations
and data delivery.

Mission Control
The  Mission  Control  is  the  core  of  satellite  operations, where  operators  monitor  satellite  health,  analyze  telem-
etry,      and      execute      commands      in      real      time.      Using      advanced      software      and      automation      tools,      the      team      ensures
mission  readiness,  efficient  scheduling,  and  reliable  communication with  ground  stations.  Focused  on  precision,
training, and resilience, Mission Control at NSSTC ensures smooth and reliable satellite operations.

Key Functions

                                                                      Data Reception
                                                                      Captures and relays satellite data back to Earth.


                                                                      Command & Control
     Key Functions                                                    Sends secure and precise commands to manage
                                                                      satellite operations.


                                                                      Telemetry Tracking
                                                                      Monitors satellite health and performance in real time.

2- The Arab Satellite 813
The         Arab Satellite 813          represents          the          first          joint          space-coopera-
tion   program   among Arab   countries,   led   by   the   United Arab   Emir-
ates  Space Agency  (UAESA).  His  Highness  Sheikh  Mohammed  bin
Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE,
announced the initiative as a contribution to the Arab Space Coop-
eration Group (ASCG).

Named         after         the        year         813,        which         marked         the         beginning         of         the
flourishing of the House of Wisdom in Baghdad under the reign of
Al Ma’mun, the satellite symbolizes a heritage of knowledge, inno-
vation, and regional collaboration. The development of the project
is    led    by    the    National    Space    Science    and   Technology Center    (NS-
STC)      at      United Arab Emirates University      (UAEU),     with      funding      by
the UAE Space Agency and UAEU.

A key educational component of the program is the Arab Space Pioneers Scholarship offered by UAEU. Through
this     scholarship,     12     students     from    various    Arab     countries     are     enrolled     in     Master’s     programs     and     are     actively
participating in the technical activities of the 813 program. Many of them completed their Master’s degree with
their thesis linked to the Arab Satellite 813 mission, underscoring the program’s strong educational and capaci-
ty-building dimensions.

In April  2025,  a  formal  System  Integration  Review  (SIR)  with  the  UAE  Space Agency verified  that  the  satellite’s
subsystems are ready to proceed to the Assembly, Integration & Testing (AIT) phase. Subsequently, the satellite
entered a comprehensive AIT campaign at NSSTC, the largest ever undertaken in the UAE, with over 30 Emirati
engineers and scientists participating. A subsequent Flight Readiness Review (FRR) confirmed system readiness
for launch. The launch of Arab Satellite 813 is scheduled for before the end of 2025.

Additionally,  during  the  May  2025 ASCG  meeting  in  Egypt, Arab  student  participants  and  the  NSSTC  technical
team   presented   updates   on   the   813   program,   demonstrating   NSSTC’s   role   in   enhancing   regional   collaboration
in the space domain.

Throughout 2025, the Arab Satellite 813 program was showcased at several prominent international conferenc-
es and exhibitions. These platforms provided opportunities to present the program’s progress, demonstrate the
scientific and environmental value of its hyperspectral data, and strengthen international and regional collabora-
tion in space research.

3- LEONAV Satellite

## PDF page 306 — continuation 2
The  Low  Earth  Orbit  (LEO)  GNSS  Navigation  satellite  (LEONAV)  program  is  designed  to  deliver  enhanced  posi-
tioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) services for ground users. This satellite system functions as an augmentation
layer  by  leveraging  signals  from  existing  Medium  Earth  Orbit  (MEO)  GNSS  constellations  and  integrating  a  new
constellation     of     LEO     satellites,     thereby     improving     overall     accuracy,     availability,     and     resilience.   The     technology
demonstrator  CubeSat  satellite,  LEONAV-1 will  receive  signals  from  existing  Medium  Earth  Orbit  (MEO)  GNSS
constellations and will transmit GNSS signals in the approved ITU Radio Navigation Satellite service (RNSS)/ Ra-
dio Determination Satellite Service (RDSS) allocated bands over the UAE. The technology demonstrator will set
the baseline for the constellation, which aims to provide positioning accuracy of <1m with 99% availability over
the targeted area. The technology demonstrator satellite is funded by the UAE Space Agency.


                                                                                                                        Mission information and Objectives:

                                                                                                                        •                                   Orbit: 510 km, SSO
                                                                                                                        •                                   Size: 12U Cube-Sat (16.3 K g)
                                                                                                                        •                                   L aunch date: Q3 2026
                                                                                                                        •                                   To transmit GNSS signals in L5/E5 and S without inter ference
                                                                                                                        •                                   To validate the transmitted signals on the ground
                                                                                                                        •                                   To                      validate                      the                      onboard                      Orbit                      Determination                      and                      Time
                                                                                                                              Synchronization (ODTS) soft ware

                                                                                                                        Partnership:

                                                                                                                        •                                   CNES and Thales Alenia Space for technical suppor t
                                                                                                                        •                                   Safran as the payload provider

## PDF page 306 — continuation 3
                                                                                                                        •                                   U-Space as the platform provider
                                                                                                                        •                                   E xolaunch as the launch par tner

Training Activities
Throughout  2025,  the  LEONAV  team  actively  enhanced  its  technical  expertise  through  participation  in  several
specialized training programs aimed at advancing knowledge in satellite navigation, remote sensing, and ground
station operations. These included:

Online Course on Remote Sensing, Satellite Technology, and Ground Station Operations (March 17-28, 2025)



306

## PDF page 307
This comprehensive program covered key principles of satellite systems, remote sensing applications, and ground
segment  operations,  equipping  participants with  practical  and  theoretical  understanding  of  end-to-end  mission
operations.

Training on Ansys STK (June 3-4, 2025, Al Ain, UAE)

Focused   on   simulation   and   mission   analysis,   this   training   enabled   participants   to   develop   skills   in   orbit   design,
system modeling, and mission planning using the industry-standard Ansys STK software.

Summer Camp Training (July 13-27, 2025, Hangzhou, China)

A hands-on international program that provided in-depth exposure to GNSS technologies, signal processing, and
satellite communication systems, fostering collaboration and knowledge exchange with global peers.

Training on GNSS Fundamentals (September 1-30, 2025, Al Ain, UAE)

This month-long course strengthened the team's foundation in Global Navigation Satellite Systems, emphasizing
positioning techniques, error modeling, and system performance analysis critical to advancing LEONAV's objec -
tives.

Together,   these   training   programs   significantly   contributed   to   the   LEONAV   team's   continuous   professional   de-
velopment and reinforced NSSTC's mission to cultivate national expertise in space and navigation technologies.

Space Science Research

1- NSSTC Planetary Science
The           Planetary           Science           Group           studies           planets
and  other  bodies  in  the  Solar  System,  including
their atmospheres and surfaces. The group uses
a      variety       of       spacecraft       data       and       mathematical
models. Their goals are the following:

•                                   E xplore,          study,          and          better          understand          the
    Solar System
•                                   Build planetar y science exper tise in the UAE
•                                   Engage universit y student s into research
•                                   Par ticipate in planetar y spacecraft missions
•                                   Raise the UAE’s visibilit y in planetar y science


The    Planetary    Science    Group    conducts    research    and    development    in    Planetary    Science    and    Exploration.   They
study   planets   and   their   environment   (their   atmosphere,  weather,   climate,   surface,   and   sub-surface).  The   group
explores  scientific  data  from  spacecraft  missions  to  planets. That  is  supported  by  mathematical  models  of  plan-
etary  environments. Also,  the  group  is  interested  in  other  bodies  in  the  solar  system  (moons,  asteroids,  ...). The
group builds expertise in planetary science in the UAE academic community, by engaging University students at
the graduate and undergraduate level.

Main themes of the group’s research:

2- Earth Observation
The Earth Observation Group (EOG) specializes
in remote sensing–based observation and anal-
ysis   of   the   Earth’s   surface.  The   group’s   primary
research focus is to enhance understanding of
surface       processes,       environmental       phenomena,
and their predictability in response to climate
change.    EOG    provides    end-to-end    expertise    —
from satellite mission concept design and pay-
load specification to downstream data process-
ing, analysis, and product development.

The    group’s    activities    are    driven    by    user    needs
and     national     priorities.     Its     first     remote     sensing
initiative    focused    on    developing    a    high-resolu-
tion, temporal land cover–land use (LCLU) mapping system to detect and monitor landscape changes over time.
This pioneering effort led to the formal establishment of the Earth Observation Group within the National Space
Science and Technology Center (NSSTC).

In addition to research, the group delivers consultancy services and generates in-house geospatial datasets that
support   evidence-based   decision-making   for   a  wide   range   of   stakeholders.   EOG   also   contributes   technical   ex-
pertise in defining payload specifications for satellite missions — such as Sat-813 — ensuring alignment between
scientific objectives and technical design.

The group pursues research in various fields of EO, which include:


•                                   Geosciences.
•                                   Farmland and vegetation monitoring.
•                                   Environment and climate change.
•                                   Sur face Hydrolog y.
•                                   Hazard zonation and disaster mitigation.
•                                   Urban sprawl monitoring.
•                                   Offshore changes and algal bloom monitoring.
•                                   Terrain Modelling, etc.
•                                   Ear th Obser vation project s include:
•                                   High Resolution L and Cover L and Use Classification of UAE
•                                   High Resolution Terrain Modelling
•                                   Impact of Climate Change on Third Pole
•                                   Sand dunes monitoring
•                                   Coral Bleaching Monitoring
•                                   Air Pollution Monitoring
•                                   Hazard Zonation Mapping
•                                   Hydro-Geomorphological Studies

Student Achievements:
The NSSTC continues to provide world-class experiential training, preparing the next generation of space scien-
tists   and   engineers   for   impactful   careers.   Since   its   inception,   the   center   has   trained   over   50   students,  with   the
majority coming from UAE universities, alongside students from other universities inside the country and inter-
national participants outside the country.

NSSTC   emphasizes   quality   over   quantity,   ensuring   that   students   receive   hands-on   experience   under   the   guid-
ance   of   expert   engineers   and   faculty   members,   contributing   to  various   space   projects   and   research   initiatives.
In  recognition  of  the  high  standard  of  training,  five  students who  completed  their  training  last year  have  joined
NSSTC as employees, contributing across different departments.


## PDF page 311 — continuation 2
The Center also offers students opportunities to present their work at local and international space conferences,
further  enhancing  their  professional  development  and  exposure. These  initiatives  underscore  NSSTC’s  ongoing
commitment to nurturing skilled talent and supporting the UAE’s growing space sector.

The   MSc   Space   Science   Scholarship   under   the Arab   Space   Pioneers   Program   (ASPP)   recruits   talented   students
from across the Arab region to join the MSc Space Science Program at UAE University and contribute to NSSTC
projects. 9 students are currently enrolled, with 2 already graduated. Their participation fosters motivation, own-
ership of learning, and a sense of community, while supporting the 813 Project’s strategic goal of engaging Arab
scientists and engineers in space science and technology.

Overview

The    world     is    witnessing     an     unprecedented     surge     in     digital     content     and     information.    This     explosive     growth     in
data  is  reshaping  research  across  traditionally  qualitative  disciplines, while  the  commercial  sector  is  being  revo-
lutionized  by  the  race  for  leadership  in  data  analytics. We  are  entering  an  era  defined  by  big  data  analytics  and
data-intensive computing, a transformation recognized globally.

Within this landscape, the UAE stands out as one of the most prepared nations in the region to embrace Big Data
technologies. Over the past two decades, the government has invested heavily in building a robust technological

## PDF page 316 — continuation 2
infrastructure, laying the groundwork for a data-driven future. Harnessing the power of big data analytics has the
potential to radically transform public services across every sector such as healthcare, medicine, transportation,
and society at large.

In    response    to    these    scientific    and    technological    imperatives,    as   well    as    the   widely    acknowledged    shortage    of
highly  skilled  data  scientists  and  analysts,  the  Big  Data Analytics  Center  (BIDAC)  has  been  established  as  an  in-
terdisciplinary hub. The center’s mission is to cultivate a new generation of researchers and scientists proficient
in big data analytics, ensuring that the UAE remains at the forefront of innovation while advancing national pri-
orities and societal well-being.

The Data Science Unit

focuses on emerging data-driven approaches, utilizing the
latest AI and machine learning technology to develop new
business models and “data” products and services.

The Big Data Technology Unit

covers            the            underpinning            mathematical,            statistical,            and
computer science research concerned with big data plat-
forms,          new          scalable          approaches          for          capturing,          storing,
managing, analyzing, and visualizing large-scale, complex,
and diverse data.

The Advisory  Board

is vital to the development of the BIDAC research agenda
and leadership. The board is responsible for the overall
well-being of the center. It provides guidance and strate-
gic input on how the center can best meet the university,
industry, and government needs.

The Scientific Board

provides  the  Centre with  independent,  impartial  scientif-
ic advice on an on-going basis and feedback and ideas
to  accelerate  the  Centre’s  development  and  the  strategic
direction. Activities also include providing suggestions to-
wards scope and choice of research topics and themes
being   pursued   in   the   context   of   the   latest   developments
and opportunities in the field.

2024:
During the academic year 2023–2024, the Big Data Analytics Center (BIDAC) successfully organized a workshop
titled    “AI-Driven    Precision    Medicine”    as    part    of    Innovation    Month.   The    event    also    featured    a    student    tutorial,
attended  by  25  university  students.  In  addition,  the  Center  conducted  two workshops  for  school  students:  “Ar-
tificial    Intelligence    and    Data    Sciences”    and    “Generative   AI    and    Its    Ethics.”    BIDAC    also    offers    an    attractive    and
highly impactful internship program., including 8 students who enrolled in the program during the academic year
2023–2024.

2025:
In 2025 Big Data Analytics Center has successfully organized a workshop titled “AI for Smart Cities: Innovation,
connectivity      and      sustainability”,    The     workshop      also      included      a      student      tutorial      in     which      7      students      from      the
university     participated.     During     the     academic    year     2024–2025,     4     students    were     trained     at     BIDAC     through     its
Internship Program, while2 students are currently undergoing training.

Strategic Goals and Objectives
Progress Towards Achieving Strategic Goals:

Continues enhancement of "The PhD Academy"
The    PhD   Academy.    Grounded    in    the    Constructivist    Learning   Theory    (CTL)    and    aligned   with    international    best
practices,  the  PhD Academy  has  successfully  graduated  236  doctoral  students  across  10  cohorts. The  program
features hands-on sessions complemented by semester-long mentorship from experienced faculty members. By
integrating   educational   theory,   gamification,   advanced   Generative  AI   solutions   (including   chatbots   and   assess-
ment    tools),    and    robust    practical    classroom    experiences,    the    PhD  Academy    offers    a    dynamic    and    empowering
environment    that    supports    the    real-world    application    of    knowledge    and    consistently    meets    or    exceeds    global
standards.

Faculty Professional Development:
CETL organized a series of Faculty Professional Development (FPD) workshops focused on critical topics such as
"Blackboard Ultra" and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Each session attracted an average of 20 participants, contribut-
ing  to  the  enhancement  of  teaching  competencies  and  instructional  effectiveness  among  UAEU  faculty  and  in-
structors. In addition, CETL facilitated a panel discussion titled “Innovations in Higher Education” and hosted Dr.
Houbing Herbert Song for an in-person session on “The Third Wave of Artificial Intelligence: Neurosymbolic AI.”

AI for Good In Education (AIGE)
AI    for    Good    in    Education    (AIGE)    is    a    forward-looking    initiative    developed    by    CETL    to    provide    educators    with

## PDF page 332 — continuation 2
practical tools and strategies for effectively integrating artificial intelligence into educational settings. This online
program    highlights    a    broad    spectrum    of    real-world   AI    applications,    delivering   valuable    insights    into    innovative
teaching   approaches,   curriculum   development,   and   methods   for   enhancing   student   engagement.   Each   session
attracts  an  average  of  75  participants. To  enrich  the  initiative,  CETL  regularly  invites  expert  speakers  from  both
academia and industry to lead virtual webinars featuring interactive, hands-on sessions, live demonstrations, and
in-depth discussions on the latest AI practices. These sessions are thoughtfully designed to empower educators
to improve learning outcomes, thoughtfully consider ethical implications, and remain at the forefront of techno-
logical advancement in education.








332

## PDF page 333
Revamp of the Peer Evaluation of Teaching (PET) Program
CETL has continued to enhance the Peer Evaluation of Teaching (PET) program through a structured two-step ac -
tion plan focused on improving assessment transparency and reliability. The updated program formally acknowl-
edges faculty excellence in teaching by aligning with internationally recognized standards and best practices. This
approach promotes ongoing teaching quality through collaborative reflection and systematic peer review.

The AI  Bootcamp
CETL conducted the AI Bootcamp, a four-day professional development program facilitated by the CETL Faculty
Fellow  to  strengthen  faculty  capacity  in  using  artificial  intelligence  for  teaching  and  learning. The  Bootcamp  in-
troduced participants to foundational AI concepts, tools, and pedagogical strategies that enhance course design,
assessment,      and      student      engagement.     Through      guided      demonstrations,      hands-on      sessions,      and      collaborative
discussions, educators gained practical experience in integrating AI responsibly and effectively into their instruc-
tional practice. Positioned within CETL’s broader AI transformation efforts, the AI Bootcamp serves as a platform
for fostering digital fluency, innovation, and forward-thinking approaches to education.

THE UAEU 3MT Competition
CETL   organized   UAEU’s   3-Minute  Thesis   (3MT),   a   university-wide   competition   designed   to   enhance   PhD   stu -
dents’    ability    to    communicate    complex    research    with    clarity    and    impact.     In    this    inaugural    season,    participants
were   challenged   to   present   their   thesis   or   research   project   in   just   three   minutes,   using   a   single   static   slide   and
language accessible to a non-specialist audience. The event provided a platform for students to refine their aca-
demic   storytelling,   strengthen   presentation   skills,   and   engage   broader   audiences   in   research   dialogue. Through
this      initiative,      CETL      continues      to      support      the      development      of      research      communication      competencies      and      to
foster a vibrant culture of scholarly exchange at UAEU.

Areas for Improvement and Future Plans:

The Design Academy
CETL is planning the Design Academy and is developing a seven-session professional development program
aimed at advancing course transformation and supporting faculty development. The curriculum integrates design
principles, creativity, and emerging AI tools to provide a progressive and engaging learning experience. Practical
resources   and   examples   drawn   from   authentic   teaching   contexts   are   being   curated   to   support   meaningful   ap-
plication,    alongside    assessment    and    reflection    strategies    to    measure    impact.   Through    this    structured    planning
process,   the   Design  Academy   is   positioned   as   a   dynamic   platform   for   fostering   design   thinking,   creativity,   and
educational innovation.

The undergraduate Academy for Critical Thinking
The CETL is in the process of establishing a dedicated academy specifically designed for undergraduate students,
focusing   on   the   development   of   critical   thinking   skills.  This   initiative   aims   to   equip   students  with   the   ability   to
analyze complex problems, evaluate evidence, and make reasoned decisions—skills that are essential for academ-
ic success and future professional endeavors.

Participants will engage with real-world scenarios that encourage active inquiry, reflective thinking, and collabo-
rative problem solving. The curriculum will integrate contemporary educational theories and proven instructional
strategies to foster a robust foundation in critical thinking. By providing these targeted resources and structured
learning  opportunities,  the  Undergraduate Academy  for  Critical Thinking will  prepare  students  to  navigate  aca-
demic challenges and contribute thoughtfully to their chosen fields.

share   best   practices,   and   engage   in   meaningful   dialogue   around   emerging   trends   in   pedagogy   and   technology.
Through these groups, CETL promotes peer learning, encourages innovation, and strengthens a culture of educa-
tional excellence and collaboration across the university and beyond.

Communities of Practice (CoPs)
The  Center  for  Excellence  in Teaching  and  Learning  (CETL)  strongly  supports  the  development  of  Communities
of Practice (CoPs) as an effective approach to knowledge management and exchange within the university. These
communities     not     only     facilitate     the     sharing     of     expertise     across     UAEU     but     also     provide     faculty     members    with
valuable opportunities to assume leadership roles and contribute their specialized skills to the broader teaching
community.

Organizational Structure
UAEU  Science  and  Innovation  Park  consists  of  four  sections  in  addition  to  the  CEO  office:  Business  Incubation
Section,      Marketing      and      Communications      Section,      Logistics      &      Operations      Section,      and      Industry      and      Business
Section



















Business Incubation Section
Business   Incubation   Section   aims   at   improv-
ing the performance of early-stage startup
nurturing             talent             and             entrepreneurial             skills,
and provision of entrepreneurial training pro-
grams. Business Incubation creates favorable
conditions    for    the    newly    established    startup
and        for        the        expansion        of        often        fragile        new
young companies.

Business Incubation leverage available amen-
ities   and   resources   such   as   office   space,   ide-
ation space and co-working space to support
young companies and early-stage startup in
the pre-implementation phase.


Marketing and Communications Section
Marketing   and   communications   section   is   responsible   for   creating   and   maintaining   a   positive   public   image   and
ensuring      effective      communication      internal      and      external      stakeholders      including      students,      faculty,      colleges,      re-
search center, industry, public and private agencies, … etc. The marketing and communication section is respon-
sible    for    developing    and    executing    marketing    strategies    to    promote    UAEU    SIP    activities,    events,    startups     and
strategic partnership with external stakeholders. This section also is responsible for developing content for social
media, websites, newsletters, and other communication channels, and collaborating with other sections and de-
partment in UAEU to ensure cohesive messaging.








346

## PDF page 347
Logistics & Operations Section

The  Logistics  and  Operations  section  is  responsible  for  the  management  of  day-to-day  operations  necessary  to
ensure a physical environment supports UAEU Science and Innovation and its internal and external stakeholders’
needs and requirements including but not limited to providing support in facility management, health and safety,
events management logistics, assets management, reception and access control service, transportation, and oth-
er related supporting services. The section collaborates with other sections and departments to ensure cohesive
and consistent alignments with UAEU procedures and process.

Industry and Business Section

The  industry  and  business  section  is  dedicated  to  create  and  strengthening  strategic  partnerships  and  collabo-
rations between UAEU and national and international corporations. It will also support companies, government
agencies, industry, funding agencies, inventors and investors interested in multidisciplinary involvement with the
UAEU. The section will also support in connecting students, faculty, research centers, inventors and startups with
companies   interested   in   advancing   their   relationships  with   UAEU   through   research,   grants,   gifts,   and   program-
matic support.

UAE Science and Innovation Park Activities & Achievements

UAEU SIP Entrepreneurship Programs

The  UAEU  Science  and  Innovation  Park  (UAEU  SIP)  has  solidified  its  commitment  to  fostering  a  robust  ecosys-
tem   of   innovation   and   entrepreneurship   by   launching   three   structured,   flagship   programs. These   initiatives   are

## PDF page 347 — continuation 4
strategically designed to support projects and startups at critical stages of their development, creating a compre-
hensive pipeline from initial idea and academic research to support full market commercialization.




                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    347

## PDF page 348
Idea-to-Prototype (I2P) Program:

An      intensive      startup      launchpad      for      entrepreneurs,      students,      researchers,      and      faculty      to      transform      innovative
ideas  into  real,  fundable  businesses. Through  hands-on  training,  mentoring,  and  customer  engagement,  partici-
pants validate their ideas, build working prototypes, and pitch to judges and investors. The program develops the
next  generation  of  entrepreneurs  and  business  leaders,  combining  speed,  practicality,  and  results. The  program
is culminating in a final Demo Day.
Key Activities:

Action-oriented       Training,        Customer        discovery,        prototyping,
and pitching.

Program Goals:

•                                   Customer validation of the business idea
•                                   Produce   MVP   (minimum   viable   product)/protot ype   in   six
    weeks that customers need
•                                   Develop and pitch the new star tup businesses during “I2P
    Demo Day”

Prototype-to-Market (P2M)
The   Prototype-to-Market   (P2M) Accelerator   Program   is   a   follow-up   to   the   I2P   program,   designed   to   transform
validated   prototypes   into   scalable,   market-ready   startups.   It   fast-tracks   entrepreneurial   growth   by   helping   par-
ticipants refine their products, build strong go-to-market strategies, and develop solid financial, operational, and
fundraising  plans. Through  continuous  customer validation  and  industry  engagement,  entrepreneurs  finalize  in-
vestor-ready pitches and business plans
Program Focus: Commercialization, manufacturing, and revenue generation.
Key Activities:  Intensive training, one-on-one coaching, and business development.
Program Goals

•                                   Develop a commercialize product
•                                   Commercialize the product (generate revenues and/or major contract s)
•                                   Deliver a professional business presentation during “P2M Demo Day”

Research-to-Commercialization (R2C)

The Research-to-Commercialization (R2C) Program is designed to help UAEU researchers and faculty accelerate
the  commercialization  of  their  research  for  greater  economic  impact  in  the  UAE  and  beyond. The  program  em-
powers  researchers  to  move  beyond  the  lab  by  translating  discoveries  into  marketable  technologies,  enhancing
the value  of  university-funded  research,  and  fostering  an  innovation-driven  culture. Through  hands-on  training,
participants conduct technology and market fit assessments, validate customers, build business models, and de-
velop clear paths to commercialization.
Program Focus: Translating academic research into market-ready technologies.
Key Activities:  Technology assessment, business model development, and investor matching.
Program Goals
•                                   Generating “business ready” technologies.
•                                   Commercialization scorecard: gaps in the business model, team, product and specific suggestions for how to
   fix it.
•                                   Top teams pitch at Deal Day.

## PDF page 348 — continuation 2
•                                   Matching top teams and local, regional and international investors.
•                                   Matching top teams and customers and par tners.
