Industry 4.0 District 4.0 Initiative:

UAEU SIP oversee the Industry 4.0 District initiative is a major strategic project conducted by UAE University as
part of its ambitious plan to be the “University of the Future”. District is inspired to integrate various components
of   the   Fourth   Industrial   Revolution   (4IR)   into   UAEU   students'   education,   including   courses,   programs,   projects,
research activities, and industrial applications.

The district supports five major themes:

•                                   Smar t Manufacturing
•                                   Cognitive, Ar tificial Intelligence and Robotics
•                                   Advanced Additive Manufacturing
•                                   Advanced Materials Characterization
•                                   Smar t Grid and Smar t Cities

Industry 4.0 District supports students, faculty, entrepreneurs, and industry partners, enabling innovation, rapid
prototyping, and commercialization of ideas that meet real-world challenges.

Highlight of activities and achievements:

•                                   3 funding programs launched
•                                   18 District 4.0 student s’ industrial project s are suppor ted
•                                   27 District 4.0 Research Project s are suppor ted
•                                   50+ Facult y Research Project s
•                                   160+ student s are involved in the research project s
•                                   15 Industr y Postdoctoral Fellowship oppor tunities are created annually
•                                   30 0+ UAEU communit y members involved in the district ac tivities



































350

## PDF page 352
The Industry 4.0 District is anchored by five state-of-the-art laboratories, each serving as a center of excellence
for a critical domain of the Fourth Industrial Revolution. These labs provide the core infrastructure for advanced
research, hands-on education, and industry collaboration, enabling students, faculty, and partners to develop and
test     next-generation     technologies.    The     labs     collectively     form     an     integrated     ecosystem     designed     to     accelerate
innovation and address real-world challenges.





Smart Manufacturing Lab

The Smart Manufacturing  Lab aims to integrate digital
technologies and intelligent automation to revolution-
ize  traditional  manufacturing  processes,  enhancing  ef-
ficiency, customization, and production speed.






Cognitive,      Artificial       Intelligence      And       Robot-
ics Lab (Cair)

The CAIR Lab focuses on the development and ap-
plication   of   advanced  AI   and   robotics   technologies   to
create intelligent systems capable of autonomous de-
cision-making and interaction with their environment.






Fablab

The  FabLab  is  dedicated  to  advancing  the  field  of  fab-
rication    technology,    utilizing    a    versatile    array    of    tools
including 3D printers, CNC machines, and convention-
al       fabrication       equipment       to       explore       innovative       tech-
niques and create complex, precise structures and ma-
terials with speed and precision.












352

Advanced Materials Characterization Lab

The Advanced   Materials   Characterization   Lab   special-
izes        in        analyzing        and        developing        new        materials       with
enhanced properties, using cutting-edge techniques to
understand material behavior at the nano and micros-
cale.






Smart Grid And Smart Cities Lab
Focusing on sustainable urban development, the Smart
Grid and Smart Cities Lab develops technologies for in-
telligent energy distribution and urban systems, aiming
to create efficient, resilient, and interconnected cities.

and    educational    spaces    designed    to    foster    teamwork,

and dedicated classrooms for hands-on training and

## PDF page 354
The Industry 4.0 District has established a comprehensive ecosystem of research programs designed to engage
the   entire   academic   community,   from   undergraduate   students   to   postdoctoral   fellows,   in   advancing   Fourth   In-
dustrial     Revolution     technologies.     Since     its     inception,     the     District     has     launched     six     distinct     research     programs,
each tailored to specific academic levels and research objectives, collectively fostering innovation, developing tal-
ent, and addressing real-world challenges aligned with the UAE's national priorities. These programs range from
student-focused     initiatives     that     provide     early     exposure     to     Industry     4.0     concepts,     to     competitive     postdoctoral
fellowships  that  attract world-class  research  talent.  Operating  across  all  UAEU  colleges  and  leveraging  the  Dis-
trict's state-of-the-art laboratories, these programs have generated a robust portfolio of projects spanning smart
manufacturing,      artificial      intelligence,      advanced      materials,      smart      cities,      and      sustainable      technologies.     Through
structured funding, mentorship, and collaboration with industry and government partners, the District's research
programs   are   cultivating   the   next   generation   of   innovators  while   producing   high-impact   research   outputs   that
strengthen the UAE's position as a global leader in technological advancement and economic diversification.

search   Office   at   UAEU,   announced   in  August   2023.  This   program   aims   to   increase   awareness   among   students
and the broader UAEU community about the applications associated with the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR).
The program provides seed money to research groups, mostly composed of students, to explore, test, and devel-
op their research ideas into solutions for real-world problems. These research groups will be mentored by faculty,
instructors, or researchers to help them develop their ideas and bring them to fruition.

collaboration with UAEU's Research Office and the Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology (MOIAT), in-
creases awareness of Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) applications among students and the UAEU community.

themes. Leveraging the Industry District 4.0 advanced laboratories, the program supports research development
and dissemination through reports, presentations, and publications while cultivating the next generation of inno-
vators driving the UAE's technological advancement and economic diversification.

The   UAEU   Postdoctoral   Fellowship   on   Industry   4.0,   launched   in   February   2025   by   the   Industry   District   4.0   in
collaboration    with     UAEU's     Research,     is     designed     to     attract     and     cultivate     top-tier     research     talent     to     drive     the
Fourth   Industrial   Revolution   (4IR).  The   program   provides   a   competitive   monthly   stipend,   health   insurance,   and
dedicated research funding to exceptional Ph.D. graduates who will work alongside a host UAEU faculty member
to   advance   cutting-edge   research   in   high-priority   domains.   Operating  within   the   university's   strategic   research
framework, the fellowship leverages the Industry 4.0 District's state-of-the-art laboratories to support the devel-
opment of novel technologies and solutions across themes such as smart manufacturing, AI, advanced materials,
and     smart     cities.    Through     the     dissemination     of     high-impact     research     in     top-tier     journals     and     presentations     at
university-wide exhibits, the initiative aims to produce significant intellectual property, strengthen industry-aca-
demia collaboration, and solidify the UAE's position as a global leader in technological innovation and economic
development and innovation.

The   Industry   4.0   District   has   strategically   invested   in   research   programs   across   multiple   colleges,   funding   a   di-
verse portfolio of projects that engage students, faculty, and researchers in cutting-edge Fourth Industrial Revo-
lution  technologies. The  following  summaries  present  the  financial  commitment,  distribution  of  supported  pro-
jects and participants, and the research outputs generated to date. With three programs currently in progress and
one under review, additional publications and research outputs are anticipated, reflecting the District's ongoing
progress in advancing innovation and developing talent aligned with national priorities.






























































366

## PDF page 367
From  September  2024  to June  2025,  Dr. Abdulrahman  Kalbat  represented  the  United Arab  Emirates  University
(UAEU) in the fifth cohort of the prestigious Government Accelerators Diploma Program. This initiative, launched
by  His  Highness  Sheikh  Mohammed   bin  Rashid Al  Maktoum,   serves  as  a  national  platform   to  address  strategic
challenges and accelerate the achievement of ambitious goals. As the UAEU representative and Project Manager
of District 4.0, he was tasked with learning world-class innovation methodologies and applying them to foster a
culture of accelerated achievement within the university, in alignment with the UAE’s national vision.

Role and Application of the 100-Day Challenge Methodology

Participation involved attending intensive workshops at the Government Accelerators headquarters and leading
a      multi-disciplinary      team      at      UAEU      to      implement      the      program’s      core      “100-Day      Challenge”      methodology.     This
framework is structured into three distinct phases: Design, Acceleration, and Sustainability. District 4.0 success-
fully  guided  the  UAEU  team  through  each  phase  to  identify  key  challenges,  set  ambitious  S.M.A.R.T.  goals,  and
deliver    tangible    results    in    a    compressed    timeframe,    thereby    translating    the    program’s    principles    into    practical,
high-impact initiatives at the university.

Phase 1 and 2: Design and Acceleration Achievements

During   the   Design   and  Acceleration   phases,   the   team   focused   on   enhancing   the   research   and   innovation   eco-
system   at   UAEU’s   Industry   4.0   District.  This   effort   culminated   in   the   successful    design   and   implementation   of
two major funding programs namely District 4.0 Research Program and District 4.0 Enablement Center Research
Program.

Phase 3: Sustainability and Scalability Initiatives

To ensure the long-term impact and scalability of the
achievements       realized       during       the       100-day       challenge,
District             4.0             initiated             two             strategic,             high-value             pro-
grams   designed   to   attract   and   retain   top-tier   research
talent     and     secure     long-term     funding     for     cutting-edge
research namely UAEU Postdoctoral Fellowship on In-
dustry 4.0 and UAEU Strategic Research Program.

The         participation         of         District         4.0         in         the         Government
Accelerators    Diploma    Program    has    been    instrumental
in  catalyzing  significant  and  sustainable  growth within
the UAEU research ecosystem. By effectively applying
the      100-day      challenge      methodology,      District      4.0      not
only achieved its immediate goals by launching two im-
pactful   research   programs   but   also   established   a   clear
pathway for long-term success through the creation of
the Postdoctoral Fellowship and the Strategic Research
Program. This experience has successfully embedded a
culture of accelerated innovation and strategic collabo-
ration at UAEU, directly contributing to the university’s
mission and the nation’s broader innovation agenda.

The Center is led by a Director reporting to the Vice Chancellor. The Center comprises of two main units:

Research & Assessment in Happiness Unit

which has the following goals:
•                                   To provide intellectual suppor t s to the Director for maintaining high qualit y of research/assessment s and
   dissemination exercises.
•                                   To identif y new oppor tunities in research collaboration and funding oppor tunities.
•                                   To ensure that all ser vices offered are fully assessed to provide comprehensive repor t s on the work
   under taken and offer improvement plan if needed.


Capacity Building and Consultancy Unit

which has the following goals:
•                                   To disseminate knowledge of mindfulness,
   happiness and positivit y via different media and
   training/retreat programs.
•                                   To develop and implement specific outreach plans/
   programs to cultivate positivit y & happiness.
•                                   To ensure that all center ser vices are accessible to
   all the segment s of the communit y.

Facilities and Infrastructure

The Emirates Centre for Mobility Research (ECMR) is equipped with state-of-the-art computational and experi-
mental facilities to support groundbreaking research. Our computational resources include a DGX1 server, which
provides exceptional processing power for developing and deploying complex AI models, and a driving simulator,
used to analyze driver behavior, evaluate advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), and simulate a wide range
of traffic conditions in a controlled environment.

The Emirates Centre for Mobility Research (ECMR) has acquired various APIs for generative AI applications such
ChatGPT,  claude,  DeepSeek  and  Gemini, which  are  utilized  in various  mobility-related  projects. These APIs  em-
power  the  center  to  conduct  research,  such  as  converting  traditional  survey  formats  into  conversational  survey
designs,   enhancing   engagement   and   data   collection.  Additionally,   they   can   be   applied   to  vision-based   mobility
projects and other innovative areas of research, enabling ECMR to remain competitive globally and stay aligned
with the latest technological advancements in transportation systems and mobility solutions.

ECMR    is    equipped    with    state-of-the-art    software    and    analytical    platforms    that    support    cutting-edge    research
in  mobility  and  transportation  systems. Among  the  key  tools  employed  are  PTV Vissim,  used  for  simulating  and
analyzing    traffic    flow    dynamics,    and    the    Bayesian    Lab,   which    enables    advanced    statistical    modeling    and    crash
analysis. The Bayesian Lab has been particularly instrumental in identifying critical factors contributing to pedes-
trian crashes in Abu Dhabi.

To     support     large-scale     mobility     modeling,     ECMR     utilizes     MATSim     for     agent-based     traffic     and     transport     simu-
lations,    allowing    researchers    to    evaluate    complex    travel    behaviors    and    urban    scenarios.    In    addition,   JeeniAI    is
used   for  AI-driven   modeling   and   predictive   analysis,   while   Claude   supports   generative   reasoning   and   research
automation.

Together,  these  advanced  facilities  empower  ECMR  to  conduct   pioneering  studies  in  trip  generation  modeling,
pedestrian crash analysis, AI-based traffic flow prediction, and the development of next-generation smart mobil-
ity solutions, reinforcing the Center’s role as a leader in data-driven transportation research in the UAE.

Strategic Goals and Progress

In 2025, the Emirates Centre for Mobility Research (ECMR) made substantial progress toward achieving its stra-
tegic goals, strengthening its position as a national hub of excellence in smart and sustainable mobility research.
Through its five active research groups and targeted interdisciplinary initiatives, the Centre continued to promote
impactful research aligned with the UAE’s priorities in innovation, sustainability, and smart urban development..

One    of    ECMR’s    key    priorities    is    to    advance    interdisciplinary    research    across    UAE    University.   The    Center    con-
tinues     to     bring     together     expertise     from     engineering,     computer     science,     and     social     sciences,     supporting     other
departments   through   technical   guidance   and   research   collaboration.  This   approach   has   strengthened   the   inte-
gration of artificial intelligence, data analytics, and advanced mobility concepts across multiple research areas.

Challenges and Lessons Learned

As the Emirates Center for Mobility Research (ECMR) continues to evolve as a leading national hub for smart mo-
bility research, the year 2025 brought both significant achievements and valuable lessons. Through ongoing sup-
port  from  UAE  University’s  leadership  and  strong  collaboration with  national  and  international  partners,  ECMR
successfully navigated challenges while identifying opportunities for strategic improvement and future growth.

Key Challenges

1. Resource and Capacity Expansion

The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence and data-intensive research has created growing demand for compu-
tational power and skilled personnel, underscoring the need for continued investment in advanced infrastructure
and research talent.

2. Data Accessibility and Integration
Access  to  high-quality,  real-time  transportation  data  remains  one  of  the  Center’s  foremost  challenges.  Effective
partnerships     with      government      agencies      are      critical      to      enhancing      data-sharing      frameworks      and      ensuring      that
research outcomes are both practical and impactful. ECMR is actively engaging with entities such as Abu Dhabi

## PDF page 391 — continuation 2
Mobility (AD Mobility), Etihad Rail, and the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure to facilitate this process.


3. Sustained Funding and Project Diversification
While  ECMR  has  benefitted  from  robust  internal  and  external  funding,  totaling    approximately AED  3  million  in
2025, there remains a need to diversify funding sources further. Expanding engagement with industrial partners,
applying for international research grants, and establishing long-term research endowments will strengthen EC-
MR’s financial resilience.




                                                                                                                                                             391

## PDF page 392
4. Interdisciplinary Coordination Across UAEU
The Interdisciplinary Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) Initiative has successfully fostered collaboration be-
tween engineering, computer science, and social science faculties. However, with increasing cross-departmental
engagement, coordination mechanisms and joint administrative frameworks must be strengthened to streamline
project delivery and enhance collective impact.

5. Global Visibility and Knowledge Dissemination
While   ECMR’s   research   output    and   conference   presence   are   commendable,   there   remains   potential   to   further
expand global visibility through high-profile partnerships, policy engagement, and public dissemination of applied
research outcomes.


Lessons Learned and Strategic Insights

1.  Value of Institutional Support
The unwavering support from UAE University’s leadership, particularly through the Office of the Associate Prov-
ost     for     Research,     has     been     instrumental     in     ECMR’s     success.     Continued     administrative,     financial,     and     logistical
backing   is   essential   to   sustain   the   Center’s   growth   trajectory   and   maintain   its   leadership   role  within   the   UAE’s
national innovation ecosystem.

2. Strength of External Partnerships
Collaborations     with      government      agencies,      private-sector      partners,      and      international      universities      have      proven
vital   in   ensuring   ECMR’s   research   remains   aligned   with    real-world   mobility   challenges.  These   partnerships,   es-
pecially with AD Mobility, Etihad Rail, the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure, and leading universities such as
Monash University, UNSW Sydney, and King Saud University, demonstrate the importance of sustained engage-
ment for impactful research delivery.

3. Human Capital Development as a Strategic Priority
The  integration  of  students  and  early-career  researchers  into  ongoing  projects  has  strengthened  ECMR’s  inno-
vation  pipeline.  Continued  investment  in  Emirati  talent  development will  ensure  long-term  national  benefit  and
knowledge continuity.

4. Data-Driven and AI-Enabled Research is Transformative
The application of Generative AI, machine learning, and simulation modeling has redefined the Center’s research
capabilities. ECMR’s experience highlights that sustained training, cross-disciplinary collaboration, and access to
modern computational tools are essential for maintaining leadership in this rapidly advancing field.


Moving Forward
Building on the insights from 2025, ECMR is committed to:
•                                   E xpanding it s infrastructure and staffing through UAEU and ex ternal funding.
•                                   Streng thening par tnerships with government and industr y to enable data-driven, policy-relevant research.
•                                   Establishing new international collaborations and competitive research grant programs.
•                                   Enhancing research dissemination through conferences, open data initiatives, and communit y engagement.

With  strong  institutional  support  and  continued  collaboration,  ECMR  is  poised  to  address  emerging  challenges

Core Values
Diversity:
We believe in creating an equitable, support-
ive,           and           diverse           environment          where           every
child,     regardless     of     their     ability,     gender,     reli-
gion, or nationality, has access to a respectful
and  nurturing  atmosphere  that  fosters  quali-
ty educational services.

Collaboration:
We foster strong partnerships between fam-
ilies, educators, researchers, and the commu-
nity       to       create       a       holistic       support       system       for
children with exceptionalities.

Innovation:
We embrace the latest research, technology, and best practices to develop forward-thinking educational strate-
gies and interventions.

Sustainability:
We      foster      a      healthier     work      environment      and      promote      continuous      growth,      nurturing      curiosity,      resilience,      and
adaptability in both children and professionals.

About the Center

The Mouza Bint Suhail Center for Exceptional Children at the United Arab Emirates University continues to play
a   leading   role   in   advancing   inclusive   education   through   the   provision   of   high-quality   assessment,   intervention,
and  educational  services  for  children with  exceptionalities. These  exceptionalities  include  giftedness,  people  of
determination, educational and learning difficulties, speech and language delays, behavioral and emotional chal-
lenges, and sensory processing or developmental disorders, not limited to these categories.

Through   this   broad   scope   of   services,   the   Center   remains   dedicated   to   addressing   the   diverse   needs   of   excep-
tional children and ensuring that every child receives individualized, evidence-based support to achieve optimal
growth and development.
The  Center  serves  children  and young  individuals  from  the  ages  of  4  to  21 years,  providing  comprehensive  ed-
ucational,    therapeutic,    and    counseling    programs    designed    to    foster    independence,    confidence,    and    leadership
among exceptional learners in a diverse and evolving society.

In June 2025, the Center reached a significant milestone with the official commencement of operations by all ap-
pointed specialists. This marked the full implementation of the Center’s multidisciplinary service model, encom-
passing  assessment,  therapy,  counseling,  and  educational  intervention within  a  unified  framework  that  ensures
integrated, high-quality support for every child and family served.

The  Center’s work  extends  across  a  wide  range  of  developmental  and  educational  areas,  including  but  not  lim-
ited   to   early   identification,   cognitive   and   behavioral   development,   communication   and   language   enhancement,
sensory integration, motor skills improvement, and emotional well-being. Through these efforts, the Center con-
tinues to uphold its mission of empowering every child to realize their full potential and contribute meaningfully
to an inclusive society.

Key Projects and initiatives

During    the    academic   year    2024–2025,    the    Mouza    Bint    Suhail    Center    for    Exceptional    Children    implemented    a
series  of  strategic  projects  and  community-driven  initiatives  that  align with  its  mission  to  advance  inclusive  ed-
ucation,  empower  children  of  determination  and  gifted  learners,  and  strengthen  collaboration with  educational
and community partners. The Center also outlined several upcoming initiatives for 2025–2026 designed to foster
innovation, creativity, and inclusion at the national level.

Outdoor Sensory Garden Project

A     therapeutic     and     educational     space     designed     to     promote     sensory     development,     motor     skills,     and     emotional
well-being for children of determination. The project, developed in collaboration with UAE University’s Facilities
Department, is currently in progress, with completion and implementation planned for 2026.











Educational Library Project

An on-site educational library was successfully established to serve the Center’s children, parents, and teachers.
The library includes a diverse collection of specialized books provided by Sharjah Library, Hudhud Publishing, and
Salwa Publishing House, creating a rich and inclusive learning environment that supports reading and continuous
learning.



















Professional Diploma for People of Determination

Developed in partnership with the College of Education, this program focuses on vocational and life-skills train-
ing    to    prepare    individuals    of    determination    for    independent    living    and   workforce    participation.  The    diploma    is
scheduled to launch in 2026.






408

Gifted and Talented Lab

An on-site educational library was successfully established to serve the Center’s children, parents, and teachers.
The library includes a diverse collection of specialized books provided by Sharjah Library, Hudhud Publishing, and
Salwa Publishing House, creating a rich and inclusive learning environment that supports reading and continuous
learning.



















Center Management System Development

In    collaboration   with    UAE    University’s    Information   Technology    Department,    the    Center    is    developing    an    inte-
grated     digital     system     to     manage     its     services,     including     case     registration,     therapy     follow-up,     and     performance
reporting. The project is currently in the planning and design phase.

National Research on Inclusive Education

 A nationwide study conducted with the Department of Special and Gifted Education at UAE University to eval-
uate     inclusion     practices     across     the     UAE.    The     research     engages     multiple     stakeholders     to     generate     data-driven
insights that inform national policy and strengthen inclusive education systems.

ent development, while strengthening partnerships that promote gifted education nationwide.

Internship Training   Programs

During the year, the Mouza Bint Suhail Center for Exceptional Children hosted 32 interns from various academic
majors    at    UAE    University.   The    interns    completed    more    than    320    hours    of    field    training    across    different    units,
gaining valuable hands-on experience in supporting children of determination.

Feedback     from     the     interns     reflected     a     4.91     out     of     5     satisfaction     rate,     highlighting     the     quality     of     supervision,
the  diversity  of  learning  opportunities,  and  the  supportive  environment  provided  by  the  Center. The  internship
program   not   only   enhanced   the   interns’   professional   competencies   but   also   contributed   to   advancing   inclusive
education practices across the UAE.

Visibility and Reach
Community Visibility

The      Mouza      Bint      Suhail      Center      for      Exceptional      Children      officially      launched      its      marketing      and      communication
activities in February 2025, marking the start of a structured strategy to enhance the Center’s visibility and com-
munity engagement. Since then, the Center has gained growing recognition through word of mouth, active social
media presence, and participation in major university and community events.

These  efforts  have  significantly  strengthened  the  Center’s  public  profile,  increased  awareness  of  its  specialized
programs and services, and reinforced its reputation as a leading institution in inclusive education and giftedness
within the United Arab Emirates.

Awareness Initiatives

During       the       academic      year       2024–2025,       the       Mouza       Bint       Suhail       Center       for       Exceptional       Children       organized       an
awareness campaign targeting parents and teachers to promote understanding and support for children of deter-
mination. The  campaign  included  the  dissemination  of  educational  posts  across  social  media  platforms  and  the
distribution of 1,200 informative brochures providing practical guidance for families and educators. This initiative
successfully    enhanced    public    awareness    of    the    Center’s    mission    and    strengthened    community    engagement    in
promoting inclusive education practices.

Strategic Goals and Objectives:

The  NWEC  focuses  on  high  quality  translational  and  applied  multidisciplinary  research  that  houses  and  coordi-
nates innovative research and activities as well as consultation services at the national, regional, and internation-
al levels in the areas of water, energy, and environment.  The NWEC strives to promote the university image as a
leading research institute in the areas of water, energy, and environment.

Notably,     the     NWEC     aims     to     pursue     holistic     and     innovative     approach     for     research,     development,     and     deploy-
ment of key technologies to generate solutions that contribute to all water-energy related domains through the
implementation    of    carefully    designed    specific    objectives.   The    members    of    the    Center    conduct    theoretical    and
applied research to better integrate water, energy, and environment and covers several research and consultancy
areas. Promoting partnerships is one of the NWEC core strategies. To that end, the center has been developing
partnerships  and  cooperation with  different  international,  regional,  and  national  institutions,  organizations,  and
governmental  entities. The  NWEC  is  keen  to  keep  its  intergovernmental  relations.  It  continued  to  work  closely
with local and regional agencies and continued to focus on emirate and federal level coordination.

The main objective of the NWEC is to provide a robust and interdisciplinary framework that can identify suitable
future development scenarios, selection criteria and intervention options resulting in more reliable, resilient, and
sustainable water resources and energy uses. The NWEC aims to pursue holistic and innovative approach for re-
search, development, and deployment of key technologies to generate solutions that contribute to all water-en-
ergy related development goals. Moreover, the NWEC contribute to advancement of the body of knowledge and
resolve   problems   related   to  water   resources,   energy,   and   environmental   systems   in   arid   and   semi-arid   regions,
and particularly in UAE. The NWEC peruse to establish and consolidate its image as one of the most prestigious
research centers at the international level in the areas of energy, water resources, and environment. The specific
objectives of the NWEC include, but may not be limited to:
•                                   Bring innovations and integrated sustainable designs to the technolog y and facilitate nature-based, broadly
   applicable solutions for water-energ y-environment related challenges to contribute to the national water
   and energ y securit y.

•                                   Provide cutting-edge research and out standing consultancy ser vices in water-energ y-environment domains
   that are informed and suppor ted by focused analysis and stakeholder engagement.
•                                   Engage stakeholders to streng then the overall ac tivities and outcomes by sharpening the understanding
   of end-user needs, regional considerations, and other data set s, while helping to identif y pathways and
   potential par tners for deployment and implementation.

•                                   Develop regional and international reputation and collaboration and provide a platform for collaborative

In addition, the Center collaborates with Visiting Scientists from McGill University and the Abu Dhabi Stem Cells
Center (ADSCC), who provide mentorship, clinical expertise, and guidance on advanced research initiatives.

Overview of the Center’s Core Scientific Divisions
1.  Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Therapeutics

Led   by   the   Center’s   research   specialists,   this   division   investigates   mechanisms   of   stem   cell   renewal,   differenti-
ation,    and    tissue    repair.    Current    research    focuses    on    mesenchymal    stem    cell    (MSC)    secretome    applications    in
neurodegenerative and inflammatory diseases.

2.  Genomic and Precision Medicine

Integrates  the  Center’s  efforts with  the  Emirati  Genome  Program  to  translate  genomic  discoveries  into  person-
alized   cell-based   therapies.  This   division   supports    collaborative   projects    in   genomic   validation   and   data-driven
regenerative applications.

3.  Translational and Manufacturing Science

Develops the infrastructure and protocols required for Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) operations, enabling
clinical-grade  cell  and  gene  therapy  production. This  division will  lead  the  Center’s  FACT  accreditation  journey,
establishing UAEU as a national reference point for regenerative manufacturing.

4.  Education, Ethics, and Policy

This division leads capacity building, public outreach, and ethical governance. It coordinates structured training,
workshops,      and      the      upcoming      UAE–McGill      Fellowship      Program      to      develop      Emirati      scientists      in      regenerative
medicine.


These     divisions     ensure     that     research,     training,     and     ethical     governance     advance     in     parallel,     reinforcing     UAEU’s
commitment to scientific excellence and national health priorities.

tional research, Emirati capacity-building, and international recognition.

## PDF page 442
Challenges

As  with  any  inaugural year,  challenges  arose  during  setup  —  but  each  obstacle  became  an  opportunity  to  build
resilience and improve operational readiness.

•                                   The Center faced challenges in recruiting and training qualified Emirati technical staff during it s initial setup;
   this was addressed through collaborations with national par tners and targeted hands-on training programs
   that successfully built local technical capacit y.
•                                   Delays in the procurement and installation of advanced equipment were overcome by close coordination
   with UAEU’s procurement office and suppliers, allowing the Center to complete full laborator y setup and
   achieve operational readiness within the first year.
•                                   Establishing standardized operational and qualit y frameworks was initially challenging, but the Center
   developed and implemented detailed SOPs and safet y protocols, creating a compliant foundation for future
   GMP and FAC T accreditation processes.

Lessons Learned

•                                   Close collaboration with established national laboratories accelerated capacit y building.
•                                   Early planning for regulator y and ethical oversight is essential for future translational research.
•                                   Gradual, stepwise development of infrastructure provides stabilit y and sustainabilit y.

Together, these lessons strengthened the Center’s operational foundation and positioned it for the translational
and educational expansion planned for 2025–2026.

Strategic Outlook (2026–2027)

As   the   Center   enters   its   second  year,   it  will   shift   its   focus   from   capacity   building   to   translational   research,   aca-
demic   growth,   and   international   engagement.   Building   on   its   foundational  year,   the   UAEU   Stem   Cell   Research
Center will transition from infrastructure establishment to translational and educational expansion. Key priorities
for 2025–2026 include:

•                                   L aunching the UAEU–McGill Fellowship in Regenerative Medicine to train Emirati scientist s.
•                                   Advancing the development of the GMP-compliant laborator y and initiating the FAC T accreditation
   process.
•                                   E xpanding the national Stem Cell Biobank to suppor t clinical and translational research.
•                                   Hosting the inaugural UAEU Conference on Regenerative Medicine (2026).
•                                   Increasing par ticipation of Emirati student s in research project s, training, and communit y education
   initiatives.

These efforts will strengthen UAEU’s role as a national and regional leader in regenerative science and innovation.

Center’s Structure

Organizational Model
ZCHS        operates        as        an        integrated       virtual        re-
search   center   that   brings   together   expertise
and resources from various colleges of UAEU.
Rather than being confined to a single build-
ing,      the      Center      functions      as      a      collaborative
network          spanning          multiple          disciplines.         The
majority        of        ZCHS        researchers        are        based        in
the    College    of    Medicine    and    Health    Scienc-
es   (CMHS),   but  we   have   active   participation
from          the          Colleges          of          Science          (COS),          Engi-
neering        (COE),        Food        and      Agriculture        (CFA),
Information              Technology               (CIT),               and               others.
This    unique    structure;    the    first    of    its    kind    in
the UAE; enables research to be conducted
across     departments     and     campuses,     leverag-
ing  diverse  laboratories  and  facilities  univer-
sity-wide.


Leadership and Governance
The Center is led by the ZCHS Director Dr. Amal AlZahmi who reports to the Associate Provost for Research. The
Director oversees strategic planning, resource allocation, and program development for ZCHS.

Affiliated Faculty and Researchers
ZCHS currently encompasses more than thirty of faculty members and researchers from various academic back-
grounds; including medicine, health sciences, public health, data science, and engineering. This multidisciplinary
team  is well-positioned  to  address  complex  health  problems  from  multiple  angles.  Faculty  join  ZCHS  as  investi-
gators on Center-funded projects or as collaborators contributing specific expertise.

Facilities and Infrastructure
ZCHS operates as a virtual center with core facilities including a 60-seat classroom, a 30- seat computer lab, two
offices for research assistants and postdocs, and access to laboratories at CMHS, CFA, COE, COS, and CIT.

Strategic Goals and Objectives

•                                   Conduct impac tful research addressing UAE healthcare priorities and establish leadership in health
    sciences regionally and globally.
•                                   Enhance infrastructure to drive innovation in health sciences, aligning with UAE’s healthcare needs.
•                                   Offer training and mentorship for student s in health sciences to develop future leaders.
•                                   Suppor t the UAE’s knowledge-based economy by translating research into prac tical applications.
•                                   Boost public awareness and international collaborations to expand the center’s influence and visibilit y.

As     ZCHS     moves     into     its     next     phase,     our     focus     is     on     expanding     our     impact     through     a     shift     toward     population
health and translational research, ensuring discoveries lead to practical solutions that benefit healthcare systems
and communities.

To  support  this  shift,  we  plan  to  strengthen  our  foundation  by  transitioning  from  a virtual  model  to  a  more  co-
hesive     physical     presence    with     dedicated     facilities     and     expert     research     teams.   This    will     enhance     collaboration,
visibility, and operational capacity.

We will also deepen interdisciplinary work across UAEU colleges and expand international partnerships to ampli-
fy research reach and relevance. At the same time, we’re investing in capacity-building through targeted training
programs to equip the next generation of researchers.

Finally,   by   stewarding   shared   data   platforms   and   infrastructure,  we   aim   to   enhance   research   quality,   efficiency,
and reproducibility. These steps are essential as we position ZCHS for national leadership and global recognition
in health research and innovation.

Challenges and Lessons Learned

In 2024–2025, ZCHS made significant strides but also encountered key challenges that shaped its future direc-
tion.


•                                     Lack of Centralized Infrastructure:  Operating as a vir tual center limited visibilit y, cohesion, and collaboration.
   This  challenge  underscored  the  need  for  a  dedicated  facilit y  to  unif y  teams,  elevate  branding,  and  enhance
   operational efficiency.
•                                     Thematic Dispersion:  Broad research ac tivit y lacked strategic focus. The new plan introduces priorit y themes
   with designated leads to build critical mass and global competitiveness.
•                              Funding Constraints: Internal   funding   was   not   sufficient   for   large-scale   initiatives.   Effor t s   are   under way   to
   increase ex ternal grant s and forge par tnerships to co-fund highimpact project s.
•                                     L   e   a   n    S   t    a   ffi   n   g    S   t   r   u   c    t   u   r   e   : Limited administrative and technical suppor t created bottlenecks. ZCHS is advocating
   for core research and coordination staff to sustain grow th and efficiency.
•                   Community Engagement Pressures:  Growing demand from key stakeholders and community partners
   highlighted the need for clear engagement protocols and translational output s. Formal MOUs and enhanced
   science communication training are now priorities.

Program Overview

Launched in 2023 under the directives of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, the Govern-
ment   Bureaucracy   Zero   Program   aligns  with   the   "We   the   UAE"  vision   to   create   the   simplest,   fastest,   and   most
efficient  government  services  globally.  UAE  University  plays  a  pivotal  role  in  this  national  initiative  by  engaging
the entire university community in eliminating administrative and academic bureaucracy.

Strategic Objectives

The program focuses on four key pillars:
•                                     Process Optimization: Restructuring operations to merge procedures, reduce documentation requirement s,
    and adopt the "one document, one time only" principle
•                                     Digital Transformation:  Eliminating digital bureaucracy through advanced systems and AI integration
•                                     Institutional Integration: Establishing seamless connec tivit y with government entities
•                                     Stakeholder Engagement: Empowering facult y, student s, and staff to drive continuous improvement

First Cycle Achievements (2023-2024)
Quantitative Impact
•                                     20 ser vices successfully streamlined
•                                     70.6% reduction  in processing time
•                                   Level 3 internal ser vices transformed

Key Initiatives
•                                     "Be a Par tner in Zero Bureaucracy" program launched to crowdsource innovative solutions from the
    universit y communit y
•                                     Zero Bureaucracy Partners Forum   hosted to streng then collaboration bet ween government entities and
    academic institutions
•                                     Communit y Training Program  delivered workshops for government institutions on ser vice transformation
•                                   Monthly newsletter and social media campaigns highlighting team achievement s

Second Cycle Progress (2025-2026)
Procedural Refinement
•                                   Work commenced in March 2025 with an updated team structure
•                                   59 procedures initially identified across all universit y sectors
•                                   Streamlined to 14 priorit y Level 1 procedures focusing on direct government integration
•                                   Comprehensive training workshops delivered on evaluation criteria and evidence collec tion

Digital Textbooks

Launched      in      Fall      2017,      the      Digital     Textbooks      Project
continues to support the United Arab Emirates Univer-
sity’s vision of becoming “The University of the Future.”
The project has successfully transformed the majority
of academic courses, replacing nearly 80% of tradition-
al   printed   textbooks   with   interactive   e-books,   leading
to over 50% savings in the allocated textbook budget.

The      integration      of    VitalSource      and      Kortext      platforms
within      the      Blackboard      Learning      Management      System
(LMS)         provides         students        with         seamless         and         cost-ef-
fective               access               to               digital               learning               resources.              These
platforms     offer     enhanced     features     such     as     offline     ac-   cess, accessibility support, and digital rights protection to
enrich  the  learning  experience.  Each  student  is  provided with  two virtual  bookshelves within  Blackboard,  auto-
matically populated with the required textbooks for their registered courses. Continuous platform enhancements
aim to improve usability and ensure alignment with evolving teaching and learning needs.

Printed Textbooks

Printed  textbooks  remain  a vital  resource  for  certain  colleges, Arabic-language  courses,  and  specific  courses  for
which e-books are not yet available. The university ensures the distribution of printed textbooks at the beginning
of     each     semester     through     dedicated     centres     serving     male     and     female     students,     faculty     members,     and    visiting
professors.

UAEU     remains     committed     to     maintaining     a     balanced     approach     between     digital     transformation     and     traditional
learning resources, ensuring equitable and inclusive access to all members of the university community.

Resource Purchase Request

Faculty,  students,  and  staff  may  request  resources  not  available  in  the  library  collection. All  submissions  are  re-
viewed and approved according to the library's policy. The libraries have fulfilled 124 title requests, totalling AED
70,586.67.

Research Support in NML

The National Medical Library continues to play a vital role in advancing research across the College of Medicine
and  Health  Sciences  by  providing  comprehensive  research  support  services  for  faculty,  students,  and  research-
ers.    Between    March    and    May,    the    NML    team    actively    participated    in    seven    systematic    reviews    as    co-authors
and provided guidance and literature support for eight student research projects. In June, the team successfully
completed   two   systematic   reviews   and   one   bibliometric    study,   followed   by   four   additional   systematic   reviews
and one bibliometric study during July–August. Support further expanded in September with contributions to ten
faculty-led systematic reviews, along with ongoing follow-up and co-authorship involvement in six postgraduate
capstone and systematic review projects.

The NML also served as a co-author in a scoping review and collaborative research project with the Department
of Medical Education. In partnership with the Department of Surgery, the library further contributed to the UAE
Randomized  Controlled Trials  (RCTs)  Project  by  assisting  in  the  identification  and  analysis  of  UAE-based  clinical
trials using systematic review methodologies.

4. Libraries Worldwide

The library has strengthened its digital services by integrating global library networks through the UAEU Library
website and the WorldCat catalogue. This integration enables our users — students, researchers, and faculty — to
discover and access a vastly expanded collection of international resources.

By connecting to WorldCat, users can locate materials held by libraries worldwide, request interlibrary loans, and
explore digital versions, all from a single platform.

This initiative enhances research efficiency, expands academic horizons, and ensures that our community bene-
fits from state-of-the-art digital information services.

•                                   Integrated LibKey Link, LibKey Nomad, and LibKey.io to improve direct access to full-tex t ar ticles from major
         databases such as PubMed, Scopus, and Elsevier.

6. Sheikh Zayed Article Archive

The     Sheikh     Zayed    Article    Archive     project     represents     a     significant     step     in     documenting     the     national     historical
narrative and preserving the media legacy of the late Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan
— may he rest in peace.

The initiative focuses on collecting, organizing, and digitally curating articles published in local, regional, and in-
ternational newspapers that highlight the life, achievements, and enduring influence of the Founding Father. All
processes are carried out internally by the library staff using the library’s own equipment and tools.

This digital archive provides researchers, students, and the wider community with a unified platform to access a

## PDF page 472 — continuation 2
rich body of historical media coverage, reinforcing the library’s role in preserving cultural heritage and supporting
scholarly research.

7. Manuscripts Project

As      part      of      the      library’s      commitment      to      safeguarding      documentary      heritage,      the      Manuscripts      Project      aims      to
systematically organize, classify, and preserve both physical (paper-based) manuscripts and digital files stored on
CDs. All operations are conducted internally by library staff using the library’s own equipment and tools.

The      project      ensures      that      rare      and      unique      manuscripts      are      accurately      documented,      stored      under      appropriate
preservation conditions, and made accessible in a structured manner for researchers and scholars. This initiative
reflects the library’s dedication to protecting cultural and academic heritage while enhancing long-term accessi-
bility.

1. Rising Employer Reputation and Improved Graduate Employment Rates
The     United   Arab     Emirates     University     (UAEU)     continued     its     upward     trajectory     in     the     QS     Employer     Reputation
Ranking, advancing from #290 in 2024 to #261 in 2025, and further improving to #229 in 2026. This sustained
progress reflects growing recognition among employers of the high calibre of UAEU graduates and the universi-
ty’s strengthened position in producing competitive national talent.

In      collaboration     with      the      Ministry      of      Education,      UAEU      conducted      the      national      graduate      outcomes      survey      to

strong response rate of 78.64%, and the semi-annual employment rate increased from 66.9% in 2024 to 76.1%
in 2025.

## PDF page 485
The   Financial   Review   provides   an   overview   of   UAEU’s   financial   performance   for   the  year   ended   31   December
2024, along with an assessment of the University’s financial position, strategy, and forward outlook. The analysis
reflects  UAEU’s  continued  commitment  to  financial  sustainability,  operational  efficiency,  and  strategic  resource
allocation.

Context

In 2024, UAEU maintained stable and effective operations supported by prudent financial management and the
continued application of flexible, student-focused operating approaches. The University grew its student popu  -
lation, with strategic prioritization of resource utilization to meet academic, research, and student service needs.
These    measures    ensured    that    UAEU    continued    to    deliver    high-quality    academic    and    research    outcomes   while
operating     within     its     financial     framework.    The     University’s     financial     and     operational     resilience     during     the     year
provides a strong foundation for long-term stability and future growth.

Going concern

The   Board   of  Trustees   confirms   that   UAEU   has   adequate   financial   resources   to   continue   its   operations   for   the
foreseeable future and, therefore, adopts the going-concern basis of preparation for the financial statements.
In   reaching   this   conclusion,   the   Board   evaluated   UAEU’s   overall   sustainability   and   the   robustness   of   the   initia-
tives supporting its strategy, considering the economic environment in which UAEU operates. The Board’s con-
fidence is supported by:

•                                   Regular assessment of UAEU’s per formance using strategic KPIs aligned with institutional sustainabilit y.
•                                   A clear focus on funding diversification and efficiency enhancement to streng then financial capacit y.
•                                   Ac tive oversight by the Audit and Risk Committee, including regular review of strategic, financial, and
            operational risks.
These  elements  collectively  ensure  that  UAEU  remains  financially  sustainable  and well  positioned  to  deliver  on
its academic mission.

Expenditure

Total expenditure for 2024 reached AED 1,671 million, reflecting a marginal increase of AED 6 million compared
to 2023.

The overall movement is mainly driven by higher staff costs and increased operational requirements aligned with
the growth in student numbers and expanding research activities.

Staff   costs   amounted   to  AED   904   million,   an   increase   of  AED   23   million   over   2023,   reflecting   ongoing   invest-
ments in academic and administrative talent.

General   and   administrative   expenses   totaled AED   531   million,   showing   a   slight   increase   of AED   2   million   from
the  previous year.

Balance Sheet

Total assets increased by AED 96 million in 2024, primarily driv-
en  by  a AED  141  million  rise  in  current  assets,  reflecting  higher
cash     balances     resulting     from     the     alignment     of     student     funding
inflows   with    the    procurement    cycle.   This    increase   was    partially
offset by a AED 45 million reduction in non-current assets, main-
ly attributable to the depreciation of Property & Equipment.

Total liabilities increased by AED 96 million in 2024, with current
liabilities      rising      by    AED      134      million,      primarily      driven      by      higher
Deferred Government Grants. In contrast, non-current liabilities
decreased by AED 38 million, largely due to reductions in Service
Concession Arrangement liabilities.

Cash Flows

Net cash flows used in operating activities increased to AED 346 million in 2024, reflecting a rise of AED 296 mil-
lion compared to 2023. This movement is primarily driven by the overall alignment between funding receipts and
operational requirements during the year. Net cash flows used in investing activities amounted to AED 74 million,
increasing by AED 62 million, mainly due to the timing of multi-year capital projects. Additionally, net cash flows
used in financing activities remained stable at AED 59 million, with no significant year-over-year movement.

Overall, the net increase in cash and cash equivalents for 2024 was AED 212 million, resulting in a year-end bal-
ance of AED 461 million compared to AED 249 million in the previous year.

## PDF page 488
Outlook

The       UAE       continues       to       demonstrate       strong       macroeconomic       momentum,       supported       by       robust       non-oil       sector
growth  and  strategic  national  initiatives  that  reinforce  economic  diversification. These  developments  provide  a
positive operating environment for UAEU.

UAEU leadership remains confident in its ability to effectively manage risks and respond to evolving financial and
operational    challenges.   The    University’s    strategic    initiatives    -    particularly    those    addressing    funding    diversifica  -
tion, efficiency enhancement, and financial sustainability - will continue to strengthen its resilience.

The current governance model allow the university to retain its earnings, contributing to a contingency and long-
term planning funding structure. This regulation emphasizes the university’s financial independence and enhance
its financial resilience.

Yet, key risks to long-term financial sustainability include:

•                                   E xposure to changes in federal funding policies.
•                                   The need to maintain high-qualit y academic infrastructure and effec tive digital capabilities with rising
   inflation.
•                                   E xposure to operational disruptions and business continuit y risks.

These risks are mitigated through UAEU’s strategic initiatives and the University’s strong governance framework,
including active monitoring by the Board of Trustees and its governing committees including Audit and Risk Com-
mittee as well as Finance, Administration, & Investment committee.

UAEU    remains    committed    to    maintaining    a    sustainable    financial    model    that    supports    academic    excellence,    re-
search advancement, and long-term institutional success.
